results_feedback: De resultatensectie is overwegend duidelijk en de gekozen analyse sluit aan bij het design. Er is een descriptieve tabel met pre- en posttestscores per conditie, en de mixed ANOVA is een passende toets voor dit ontwerp. Ook worden hoofdeffecten, interactie-effect en post-hocvergelijkingen gerapporteerd, wat positief is. De tekst benoemt de kernbevindingen duidelijk en koppelt deze correct aan de hypothesen. Tegelijk zijn er enkele problemen. De rapportage wijkt af van het voorbeeldniveau uit de cursus: er ontbreekt een demografische tabel, de assumptiecheck is summier en deels onnauwkeurig geformuleerd (bijvoorbeeld 'Shaprio-Wilk-assumptie' en 'homogeniteit van variaties'). De rapportage van de post-hoc t-toetsen is ook wat vreemd, omdat dezelfde vrijheidsgraden voor binnen-conditievergelijkingen worden gebruikt en niet helemaal duidelijk is hoe deze toetsen precies uit de ANOVA volgen. Verder is Figuur 1 wel genoemd maar niet echt opgenomen in de tekst zoals gepresenteerd. Ondanks deze onvolkomenheden is de analyse voor dit niveau grotendeels coherent en relevant, dus een voldoende tot goede beoordeling is passend.
discussion_feedback: De discussie is een sterk onderdeel van het paper. De eerste alinea geeft een heldere hoofdconclusie, beantwoordt de onderzoeksvraag en benoemt expliciet dat de hypothese slechts gedeeltelijk wordt ondersteund. Daarna worden de resultaten goed vergeleken met eerder onderzoek en wordt het onverwachte resultaat — dat VRET effectiever was dan IVET — serieus genomen in plaats van genegeerd. Positief is ook dat de student meerdere mogelijke verklaringen bespreekt, waaronder ervaren controle, aansluiting bij adolescent-specifieke kenmerken en verschillen in begeleiding. De sectie laat daarmee echte wetenschappelijke redenering zien. Daarnaast is er relevante kritische reflectie: de mogelijke confound van verschillen in begeleiding wordt benoemd, en toekomstig onderzoek wordt logisch uit deze beperking afgeleid. Wel zijn sommige interpretaties nog wat speculatief en worden niet alle verklaringen even scherp afgewogen. Ook is de redenering rond het 'geen confound want klinische praktijk' inhoudelijk niet helemaal overtuigend: juist voor interne validiteit blijft dit wel degelijk problematisch. De koppeling terug naar de theorie is aanwezig maar had nog explicieter en systematischer gekund. Desondanks is dit een overtuigende, bovengemiddelde discussie.
lang_style_feedback: De tekst is over het algemeen goed leesbaar, duidelijk gestructureerd en passend wetenschappelijk van toon voor dit niveau. De opbouw per sectie is logisch en de lezer kan de rode draad meestal goed volgen. De student gebruikt doorgaans heldere formuleringen en signaleert verwachtingen, resultaten en interpretaties redelijk expliciet. Er zijn wel meerdere taal- en stijlproblemen die een hogere score in de weg staan. Er komen geregeld spelling- en formuleringfouten voor, zoals 'verassend' in plaats van 'verrassend', 'Axiety', 'als.' en enkele onhandige of lange zinnen. Ook zijn er APA-onvolkomenheden en inconsistenties in referenties en jaartallen, bijvoorbeeld Bouchard 2017/2016 en het gebruik van Kampmann et al. (2016). Sommige zinnen zijn wat redundant of grammaticaal stroef. Deze fouten verstoren het begrip niet ernstig, maar maken de afwerking minder sterk dan bij een echt goede taal/stijlscore.

intro_feedback: The introduction clearly states a relevant research question and hypotheses, addresses societal relevance early, and defines key concepts such as SAS, IVET, and VRET. It also includes the required body of literature in substance, including the core VRET/SAD studies and an adolescent-focused self-found article. The overall line of reasoning is understandable and broadly logical: SAS is important in adolescents, IVET has limitations, VRET may overcome some of these, and adolescent-specific characteristics may make VRET especially promising. This is enough for Tier 2. The main limitation is that the literature use is not always fully accurate or optimally connected. One of the required core articles is misrepresented/replaced: Kampmann et al. (2016) is cited in the text as support for VRET but in the reference list it is a meta-analysis rather than the required RCT, and Bouchard is listed as 2016 in the references while discussed as 2017. The theoretical framework is present, mainly via the maintenance cycle of social anxiety and the role of control/self-confidence in VRET, but it remains somewhat loose and is not consistently developed into a tight argument. Prior studies are connected better than in a pure article-by-article summary, yet the introduction does not fully use them as cumulative building blocks, and the explicit justification of the chosen three-arm design could be stronger. Because the reasoning is adequate and at points quite good, but not consistently convincing enough for full Tier 3, a 7.0 is appropriate.
methods_feedback: The Methods section is coherent with the stated research question and includes Participants, Materials, and Procedure. The participant description gives sample size, age, SD, gender distribution, allocation to conditions, and clear inclusion/exclusion criteria. The design is understandable and broadly replicable at this student level. The LSAS-CA is described with reference, number of items, example content, response scale, score range, and interpretation, which fits Tier 2 well. The procedure is chronological and covers all three conditions from start to finish. However, several expected details are missing or underdeveloped. Compensation/reward is not mentioned, which prevents a stronger Tier 2 performance. The independent variable manipulation is only partly described: VRET hardware is reported, but the actual content of the virtual social scenarios and how VRET and IVET were standardized across conditions are not explained in enough detail. The IVET condition description also raises some ambiguity because it is said to be conducted 'zelfstandig' outside the lab during the session, which is understandable but not very precise. Information is sometimes compressed into dense paragraphs and the Materials section lacks fuller descriptions of both treatment conditions as manipulations. Because the section meets Tier 2 core criteria overall but not the more complete detail and placement standards of Tier 3, 6.5 is justified.
results_feedback: The Results section reports an analysis that is appropriate for the design: a mixed ANOVA with time as within-subject factor and condition as between-subject factor. Main effects and the interaction are reported with F values, degrees of freedom, p values, and effect sizes, and descriptive statistics are given at the operational level for LSAS-CA scores. Post-hoc tests are also included and interpreted in line with the hypotheses. This is clearly above passing. It also mentions outliers and assumption checks, and includes a table and figure in principle. That said, the section does not reach Tier 3. The demographic information per condition is missing from a results table, which is explicitly expected at Tier 2; however, enough core statistical reporting is present that the section still fits the lower end of adequate overall. Assumption reporting is too limited and partly imprecise: Shapiro-Wilk is mentioned, but no actual values are given, and 'homogeniteit van variaties' is reported vaguely. With only two time points, sphericity is not relevant, but this is not explicitly explained. The outlier decision is stated, but the rationale is informal and no method is specified. The post-hoc reporting is reasonably complete, though some values and df choices are unusual and not fully transparent. The figure and table formatting are also much less developed than in the sample results section. Overall, this is a workable and understandable Results section at about Tier 2 level, so 6.5 fits best.
discussion_feedback: The Discussion is the strongest section of the paper. It clearly revisits the aim and hypotheses, states the main conclusion, and interprets the findings at construct level rather than merely repeating numbers. The student does more than note that VRET outperformed IVET: they actively try to explain why this happened, connect the finding to adolescent-specific mechanisms, and discuss whether the result reflects virtuality itself or differences in therapeutic guidance. This shows solid scientific reasoning for this level. Prior research is used substantively rather than only name-dropped, and the discussion returns to the theoretical ideas introduced earlier, such as avoidance, self-focused attention, control, and confidence. Study-specific limitations are discussed with reasonable depth, especially the unequal level of therapist guidance as a possible confound. Future research directions are specific and logically follow from the limitations, including a four-condition design separating virtuality from guidance and examining long-term effects. Broader implications for youth mental health care are also addressed. The section reaches Tier 3 because the reasoning is coherent, comparisons to previous work are substantive, and limitations are linked to their impact on conclusions. It does not quite reach Tier 4 because the discussion still reads somewhat extended and repetitive in places, and some claims about clinical implications are a little stronger than the design fully supports. A 7.5 is therefore appropriate.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally readable and scientifically framed, and the overall structure is clear enough to follow. Most paragraphs have a discernible focus, and terminology is mostly used consistently. This supports a Tier 2 score. However, there are enough language and presentation issues to keep the score at the lower end of adequate. There are multiple spelling/typing errors and awkward phrasings (for example 'Axiety', 'verassend', 'bloostelling', inconsistent spacing and punctuation, and some sentence-level grammatical problems). APA and reference accuracy are also uneven: there are inconsistencies in years/authors for core studies, some formatting problems in the reference list, and occasional citation inaccuracies. In the Results section, formatting of the table/figure labels is rough, and section transitions are acceptable but not especially smooth. Still, the language does not seriously obscure meaning, and the paper remains understandable throughout. Because the writing is competent but clearly not near-faultless, 6.5 is the best fit.

intro_feedback: The introduction clearly states a relevant research question and explicit hypotheses, addresses societal relevance early, and defines key concepts such as SAS, IVET, and VRET. It includes the required literature base in substance, but there is an important mismatch with the prescribed core articles: Anderson et al. (2013) and Bouchard et al. are included, but Kampmann et al. (2016) is not actually discussed as the required RCT on VR social interaction exposure; instead Kampmann et al. (2015) is discussed, while the listed 2016 paper in the references is a meta-analysis. Because the rubric requires the 3 core articles plus 1 self-found article, this weakens the score. Beyond that, the line of reasoning is generally understandable and mostly logical: societal relevance leads into theory about avoidance and self-focused attention, then into treatment logic and prior VRET/IVET findings, and finally into the adolescent-specific gap. The student does more than summarize by connecting studies to the hypothesis, especially when arguing that adolescent developmental characteristics may make VRET relatively more suitable. Scientific relevance is argued, not merely mentioned. However, the theoretical framework is somewhat limited: it is present, but not very explicitly structured as a framework linking IV, DV, and mechanism, and parts of the literature integration remain somewhat study-by-study. The design choice is justified, but not especially sharply tied to specific prior-study limitations. This fits Tier 2 overall rather than Tier 3.
methods_feedback: The methods section is broadly coherent with the stated RQ and hypotheses, and all major subsections are present. The participants section reports sample size, age, SD, gender distribution, inclusion and exclusion criteria, and random allocation to conditions. The materials section describes the main outcome measure with developer reference, number of items, examples, response scale, scoring range, and interpretation of scores. The procedure is chronological and covers all three conditions from start to finish. These elements satisfy the core of an adequate methods section. However, several details prevent a higher score. Compensation/reward is not mentioned, even though this is expected at Tier 2. The intervention descriptions are not sufficiently detailed in the Materials section: VRET hardware is described, but the actual content of the VRET and IVET manipulations, what social scenarios were used, how sessions were standardized, and what exactly differed between conditions are only partially clear and are spread across sections. Important intervention detail is left somewhat vague, making replication difficult. Also, the procedure contains material-level content, and there is no separate analyses subsection. The choice to let IVET occur partly outside the lab is explained, which is a strength, but standardization and confound-prevention are not well specified. Overall this is adequate but not strong: enough detail for coherence, not enough for a solid Tier 3.
results_feedback: The results section identifies an appropriate analysis for the design (factorial mixed ANOVA), reports the main effects and interaction with test statistics, p-values, and effect sizes, and presents descriptive statistics at the operational level. A table with pre/post means and SDs is included, and post-hoc tests are reported with Holm correction. This satisfies the main Tier 2 expectations in broad terms. However, there are notable weaknesses that keep the score at the lower end of adequate. The demographic table expected by the rubric is missing; participant characteristics are only given in Methods. The outlier handling is mentioned, but not in the clearer style of the sample results, and the rationale is rather brief. Assumption checks are underreported or inaccurately phrased: normality and homogeneity are mentioned, but not with proper detail, and for a repeated-measures design there is no real treatment of assumptions at the level expected by the guide/sample. The statement that the Shapiro-Wilk assumption and homogeneity of variances were met is also too compressed to evaluate properly. The figure is referred to but not actually present in the submitted text as a readable figure. There are also some inconsistencies and oddities in the inferential reporting (for example identical dfs for all within-condition post-hoc t-tests, and somewhat unclear wording around posttest comparisons), which reduces confidence in correctness. Still, the section is recognizably structured as a results section and covers the core findings sufficiently for this level.
discussion_feedback: The discussion is the strongest section of the paper. It clearly revisits the aim and hypotheses, states that the hypothesis was partly rejected, and interprets the main findings at the construct level. The student compares the findings to prior research and does more than simply note agreement/disagreement: the discussion explains that both treatments being effective aligns with prior work, while VRET outperforming IVET is unexpected relative to previous adult and adolescent findings. The student then develops possible explanations, including adolescent-specific fit of VRET and differences in therapeutic guidance. The theoretical ideas from the introduction, especially avoidance, self-focused attention, control, and confidence, are revisited and used to interpret the findings. There is also a meaningful critical evaluation: the discussion correctly identifies that differences in guidance may act as an alternative explanation and potentially introduce a second variable, and it proposes a concrete four-condition follow-up design to disentangle guidance from virtuality. Broader practical implications for youth mental health care are also addressed. The main reason this does not rise higher is that the discussion occasionally overstates what can be concluded, and the treatment of the guidance issue is somewhat inconsistent: it is recognized as a possible confound, but later partly dismissed because it resembles clinical practice, which does not fully resolve the internal validity concern. Also, there is less explicit evaluation of the theoretical framework as a framework than a stronger Tier 3/4 discussion would have. Still, this is a coherent, substantive, and above-average discussion.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally clear, readable, and organized into recognizable scientific sections. Most paragraphs have a discernible focus, terminology is mostly used consistently, and the writing usually supports the argument rather than obstructing it. The overall structure is coherent, especially in the introduction and discussion. At the same time, there are several language and APA-level issues that prevent a higher score. There are noticeable spelling/typing problems (for example 'verassend', 'Axiety', 'Shaprio-Wilk', missing spaces, and some awkward phrasing), formatting inconsistencies in headings and tables, and multiple reference inaccuracies or inconsistencies (e.g., Bouchard year mismatch in text/reference list, Kampmann 2016 cited in a way that does not match the discussed study, inconsistent capitalization and formatting). Some sentences are overly long or slightly clumsy, and a few transitions are less smooth than they could be. These issues are not severe enough to undermine comprehension, but they are too frequent for Tier 3. Overall, the paper fits solidly within adequate language and style.

intro_feedback: De introductie voldoet duidelijk aan Tier 2. De onderzoeksvraag is impliciet maar voldoende helder: of VRET effectief is voor adolescenten met SAS en hoe dit zich verhoudt tot IVET en een wachtlijst. De hypothesen zijn expliciet geformuleerd. Maatschappelijke relevantie is goed aanwezig en ook redelijk afgestemd op adolescenten. Er is een theoretisch kader aanwezig rond vermijding, zelfgerichte aandacht en de vicieuze cirkel van sociale angst, en dit wordt gebruikt om VRET te motiveren. Ook is wetenschappelijke relevantie beargumenteerd via het gebrek aan onderzoek bij adolescenten. De literatuur wordt deels met elkaar verbonden en niet alleen los samengevat. Wel blijven er enkele beperkingen die Tier 3 net niet volledig ondersteunen: de drie verplichte artikelen zijn niet allemaal correct gebruikt zoals voorgeschreven in de cursuscontext (Anderson et al. wordt niet inhoudelijk besproken, Kampmann 2016 wordt in de tekst niet als de vereiste RCT gebruikt, en Bouchard wordt als 2017 besproken maar in de referentielijst staat 2016), de argumentatielijn is overwegend coherent maar niet overal strak, en de designkeuze wordt pas laat expliciet verantwoord. De introductie is daarmee adequaat tot bovengemiddeld, maar nog niet overtuigend genoeg voor een stevige 7.5+.
methods_feedback: De methodesectie haalt Tier 2 net. De deelnemerssectie bevat steekproefgrootte, leeftijd, SD, genderverdeling, inclusie- en exclusiecriteria, en random toewijzing aan condities. De procedure is chronologisch en sluit aan op de onderzoeksvraag. Ook wordt het algemene verschil tussen condities duidelijk beschreven. De sectie heeft echter meerdere tekortkomingen die een hogere score verhinderen. Belangrijke verplichte details ontbreken of zijn summier: compensatie/reward wordt niet genoemd, de materialen zijn beperkt uitgewerkt, en slechts één vragenlijst wordt echt volledig beschreven. De onafhankelijke variabelen zijn niet in gelijke mate uitgewerkt: VRET krijgt een technische beschrijving van de headset, maar de inhoud van de virtuele scenario’s en de concrete standaardisatie tussen VRET en IVET blijven vaag. Voor IVET wordt onvoldoende precies uitgelegd welke sociale opdrachten werden uitgevoerd. Er is ook geen aparte analyseparagraaf. Daardoor is de sectie coherent en voldoende voor dit niveau, maar niet volledig genoeg voor Tier 3.
results_feedback: De resultatensectie voldoet aan Tier 2, maar vrij aan de onderkant. Positief is dat de juiste globale analyse is gekozen voor het design (factorial mixed ANOVA), de kernresultaten met F-waarden, p-waarden en interactie worden gerapporteerd, en er zijn gemiddelden en standaarddeviaties per conditie en tijdstip. Ook worden post-hocvergelijkingen en effectgroottes genoemd. Toch ontbreken meerdere onderdelen die volgens het rubric en voorbeeld nodig zijn voor een sterkere score. Er is geen demografische tabel per conditie. Er is wel een verwijzing naar een figuur, maar in de ingeleverde tekst is de figuur zelf niet zichtbaar uitgewerkt. De assumptiecontrole is erg summier en deels onnauwkeurig geformuleerd (Shapiro-Wilk voor normaliteit en 'homogeniteit van variaties', zonder verdere specificatie). De outlier-rapportage is beperkt en geeft geen duidelijke onderbouwing op het niveau van het voorbeeld. Verder zitten er enkele inconsistenties en onnauwkeurigheden in de interpretatie, bijvoorbeeld 'zoals verwacht' bij een effect dat elders juist afwijkt van de hypothese, en de rapportage van post-hoc t-toetsen is niet altijd volledig overtuigend gekoppeld aan het design. Daarom passend als adequate maar niet sterke results score.
discussion_feedback: De discussie is het sterkste onderdeel en voldoet aan Tier 3. De onderzoeksvraag en hypothese worden direct hernomen, de hoofdconclusie is duidelijk, en alle hoofdbevindingen worden op constructniveau geïnterpreteerd. De student vergelijkt de bevindingen inhoudelijk met eerder onderzoek en legt zowel overeenkomsten als verschillen uit. Vooral het onverwachte resultaat dat VRET effectiever was dan IVET wordt serieus besproken en er worden meerdere mogelijke verklaringen gegeven, waaronder ervaren controle, adolescent-specifieke kenmerken en verschillen in therapeutische begeleiding. De theoretische lijn uit de introductie wordt ook weer opgepakt. Daarnaast bevat de discussie meerdere studiespecifieke beperkingen en concrete voorstellen voor vervolgonderzoek, waaronder een sterk vier-condities design om begeleiding en virtualiteit uit elkaar te trekken. De maatschappelijke/praktische implicaties voor de jeugd-GGZ worden ook teruggekoppeld. Waarom geen 8.0 of hoger: sommige redeneringen zijn nog speculatief en niet altijd goed afgebakend van wat echt door de data wordt ondersteund; bovendien wordt het punt over begeleiding eerst overtuigend als mogelijke confound besproken maar later deels gerelativeerd, wat de argumentatieve scherpte iets vermindert. Toch is dit voor dit niveau een goede, bovengemiddelde discussie.
lang_style_feedback: De tekst is over het algemeen duidelijk, goed leesbaar en wetenschappelijk van toon, passend bij Tier 2. De opbouw per sectie is herkenbaar en de meeste paragrafen hebben een duidelijke focus. Er is redelijk consistente terminologie en de argumentatie is meestal goed te volgen. Er zijn wel vrij wat kleine taal- en stijlfouten, zoals typefouten ('verassend', 'bloostelling'), enkele kromme zinnen, inconsequente verwijzingen naar artikelen/jaren, en wat slordigheden in opmaak en APA-stijl. Ook zijn sommige zinnen lang of licht redundant. Dit verhindert een Tier 3-score, maar het geheel blijft duidelijk voldoende tot degelijk.

intro_feedback: The introduction presents a clear and relevant research problem, starting with societal relevance and then narrowing toward the comparison between therapist-guided and self-guided VRET for SAD. The overall line of reasoning is coherent: SAD is prevalent and impairing, treatment exists but has barriers, VRET may reduce some barriers, and self-guided VRET may reduce them further. The research question and hypothesis are clearly stated and logically connected to the preceding literature. The student also uses the required core VRET studies appropriately as building blocks and adds an extra relevant article on self-guided VRET. What keeps this from the higher range is that the theoretical framework is only partly developed. The discussion of exposure therapy and Pavlovian extinction gives some theoretical grounding, but the argument for why therapist guidance should outperform self-guided VRET is relatively brief and not strongly theorized beyond lack of feedback. There is also more summary than true synthesis in places, and some article details/citations are inconsistent with the course materials (e.g., year differences for Kampmann and Bouchard). Still, for this level, the introduction is clearly above average and convincingly motivates the study.
methods_feedback: The method is coherent and aligned with the stated research question and hypothesis. Participants, inclusion/exclusion criteria, allocation, compensation, materials, and procedure are all present. The design is understandable and in principle replicable for this student level. Strengths include clear reporting of sample size, age, gender breakdown, random assignment, basic exclusion criteria, and the repeated-measures structure. The LSAS-SR is described with developer reference, item count, scale, example items, score range, and psychometric support, which fits the guide well. The main limitations are that some details remain vague or underdeveloped. For example, the intervention itself is described rather generally, with limited detail about the exact treatment protocol, the content of the six sessions, and how equivalence between conditions was ensured beyond broad statements. It is also somewhat unclear how diagnosis was implemented procedurally, by whom SCID-5 was administered, and whether the take-home self-guided condition was monitored for adherence. The procedure also contains a bit of overlap with materials. Overall, the section is complete and mostly correct, but not detailed enough for a stronger grade.
results_feedback: The results section is mostly correct, relevant, and understandable for the stated mixed design. The student reports descriptive statistics across conditions and time points, includes the main ANOVA, reports the interaction, and follows up with post-hoc comparisons that address the hypothesis and pattern over time. The write-up clearly communicates the main findings, especially the stronger immediate effect for therapist-guided VRET and the convergence at follow-up. This matches the expected structure reasonably well. However, the section is somewhat below the sample's level in completeness and presentation. A demographics table is missing, and the descriptive table is somewhat awkwardly formatted. Assumption checks are reported only generally, without much detail, and the outlier handling is noted but not justified in a particularly analytical way. There are also some imprecise phrases and small reporting inconsistencies. Still, the analysis is coherent and appropriate for this level, so this is an adequate-to-good results section rather than an excellent one.
discussion_feedback: The discussion gives a correct and mostly coherent interpretation of the results. It begins with a clear answer to the research question, states that the hypothesis was supported for post-treatment, and accurately summarizes the main pattern including the convergence at follow-up. The student relates the findings back to prior literature and makes a reasonable attempt to explain both expected and unexpected findings, especially the delayed improvement in the self-guided condition. The discussion also includes several study-specific limitations, such as contextual differences in questionnaire completion, generalizability issues due to the student sample, and possible context effects of treatment location. These limitations are relevant and tied to future research suggestions. What limits the grade somewhat is that the discussion of theory is not very deep. The explanation using self-efficacy is plausible, but it is somewhat speculative and not tightly integrated with the theoretical framework built in the introduction. The section also could have done more to discuss what the findings mean for the extinction-based account or for the role of therapist support more conceptually. Practical implications are present, but somewhat stronger than the limitations fully justify. Overall, this is a solid above-average discussion for this course level.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally readable and the structure is clear, with recognizable sections and a mostly logical flow. Scientific language is mostly appropriate, and the main ideas are understandable throughout. However, there are quite a few language and APA/style issues that prevent a higher score. These include grammar problems, awkward phrasing, punctuation/spacing inconsistencies, inconsistent capitalization and hyphenation (e.g., selfguided/Selfguided/self-guided), occasional unclear wording, and multiple reference inaccuracies. There are also some APA issues in citations and references, such as formatting inconsistencies, unusual entries, and small errors in article details. Paragraphing is mostly functional, but some sentences are repetitive or clunky. These issues do not seriously obstruct comprehension, but they are frequent enough to place the paper in the adequate range rather than clearly good.

intro_feedback: The introduction presents a clear and relevant research problem and builds a mostly coherent line of reasoning toward the research question and hypothesis. The paper starts with societal relevance, explains SAD and its consequences, discusses existing treatments, and then narrows to exposure therapy, VRET, and finally self-guided versus therapist-guided VRET. This hourglass structure fits the writing guide well. The research gap is clearly identified: there is no direct comparison between therapist-guided and self-guided VRET. The hypothesis is explicit and aligned with the proposed design. The student also uses the required core VRET studies and an additional article relevant to the self-guided focus. However, the argumentation is stronger as a sequence of summaries than as a fully integrated synthesis. The theoretical framework is present only in a limited way: extinction learning is mentioned, and lack of therapist feedback is briefly used to justify the hypothesis, but the theory is not developed in much depth and the link between theory, design, and expected long-term effects could be more explicit. There are also some citation/year inconsistencies relative to the course materials and some imprecise phrasing. Overall, this is a solid, above-average introduction with a clear RQ and relevant motivation, but not yet fully convincing at the level of a highly integrated theoretical argument.
methods_feedback: The method section describes a coherent study design that matches the stated research question and hypothesis. Participants, inclusion/exclusion criteria, random assignment, compensation, materials, and procedure are all present. The design is easy to follow and the repeated-measures comparison between therapist-guided and self-guided VRET is clearly connected to the hypothesis. Important sample characteristics are reported, including mean age, SD, gender distribution, and sample size per condition. The intervention conditions are described in a reasonably comprehensible way, and the LSAS-SR is described with developer reference, number of items, response scale, score range, example items, and brief psychometric support, which is good for this level. The section is not fully complete or precise enough for a higher grade, though. Some procedural details remain vague for replication, such as how exactly the virtual therapist operated, what specific scenarios were used, how therapist guidance was standardized across participants, and whether diagnostic assessment and outcome measurement were administered blinded or not. The analysis plan is also not explicitly described in the methods, appearing only in the results. There is some mixing of procedural and materials information, and the design introduces contextual differences between conditions that later become a discussion limitation. Still, for a second-year student paper this is a solid and mostly complete methods section.
results_feedback: The results section is mostly correct, complete, and clearly related to the stated design. It includes descriptive statistics for the main outcome across conditions and time points, and the reporting of the mixed ANOVA matches the repeated-measures two-condition design. The main effects and interaction are reported clearly, and the post-hoc comparisons are used appropriately to interpret the interaction. The narrative interpretation is understandable and stays at the operational level of LSAS-SR scores. This follows the general structure expected from the sample results and is around the expected baseline or slightly above. The section is somewhat weakened by the absence of a separate demographics table, which the guide and sample expect, and by limited detail in the assumption checks: assumptions are said to be met, but the specific tests/statistics are not reported. Reporting around outliers is also somewhat inconsistent, since outliers are noted but not further justified statistically. There are also minor APA/statistical formatting issues. Nevertheless, the analyses are coherent, relevant, and sufficiently complete for this course level.
discussion_feedback: The discussion gives a clear main conclusion that answers the research question and states that the hypothesis was supported at post-treatment. It interprets the key pattern in the data reasonably well: therapist-guided VRET outperformed self-guided VRET immediately after treatment, but the groups converged at follow-up. Importantly, the student does not ignore the unexpected follow-up pattern in the self-guided condition and tries to explain it, which is a strength. The discussion also reconnects findings to prior research and appropriately highlights what this study adds compared to previous VRET studies. Several study-specific limitations are discussed, especially the difference in questionnaire context across conditions, the restricted student sample, and the possible role of treatment context. These limitations are relevant and convincingly argued, and future research suggestions follow logically from them. The section is not excellent because the theoretical implications remain somewhat underdeveloped: the discussion does not return in a sustained way to the extinction framework or build a clear theory-based interpretation of why effects differed over time. Some interpretations are plausible but somewhat speculative, especially the self-efficacy explanation, and the broader societal implications could be more carefully qualified in light of the limitations. Still, this is a good and above-average discussion for this level.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally readable and uses mostly appropriate scientific language. The overall structure is clear, with recognizable sections and mostly understandable paragraph organization. The argument is usually easy to follow. However, there are frequent language and APA-style issues that lower the score somewhat. These include grammatical errors, awkward phrasing, punctuation problems, inconsistent capitalization and hyphenation (e.g., selfguided/self-guided, therapistguided/therapist-guided), spacing issues, and several citation/reference inconsistencies. There are also some imprecise or informal formulations and a few redundant passages. The reference list contains noticeable APA errors and inconsistencies in formatting. These problems do not seriously impede understanding, but they are too frequent for a higher style grade. Overall, the language and style are adequate but clearly not polished.

intro_feedback: The introduction presents a clear and relevant research problem and generally follows a logical line toward the research question. It opens with societal relevance, explains SAD and treatment need, and motivates interest in VRET as a potentially more acceptable alternative to in vivo exposure. The research question and hypothesis are clearly stated, and the paper uses the required core literature responsibly while adding an additional relevant article on self-guided VRET. The overall argument is coherent and appropriate for this course level. The main limitation is that the theoretical framework is somewhat underdeveloped. The Pavlovian extinction model is mentioned, but the introduction does not build a fuller theory explaining why therapist guidance should matter specifically, or why differences might emerge immediately versus over time. Some literature use is more summary-like than synthetic, and the transition from therapist-guided VRET effectiveness to self-guided VRET could be argued more sharply. There are also some inaccuracies relative to the course materials (e.g., years of the focal studies differ from the prescribed ones), but the studies are still used meaningfully. Overall, this is a good, above-average introduction with a clear storyline, though not fully convincing at the level of theoretical integration and synthesis needed for a higher grade.
methods_feedback: The methods section is coherent and clearly linked to the stated research question and hypothesis. Participants, materials, and procedure are all present, and the basic design can be understood and in broad terms replicated. The section includes sample size, age, gender distribution, inclusion/exclusion criteria, random assignment, compensation, treatment length, measurement moments, and the main outcome measure. The LSAS-SR is described with number of items, scale, example content, score range, and psychometric support, which is a strength. The main weaknesses are incompleteness and some lack of precision in key procedural details. Recruitment is described only broadly, with limited detail on how students were approached or screened beyond SCID-5 diagnosis. The intervention description remains somewhat vague: the exact content of the VR scenarios, how exposure hierarchy was built, what the virtual therapist said or did, and how therapist guidance was standardized are not specified in enough detail. There is also no separate analysis subsection, which is typically expected in a full methods section, even though the analysis is later described in Results. In addition, some design choices that may introduce confounds—especially home-based self-guided treatment versus office-based therapist-guided treatment—are described but not justified in Methods. Overall, this is a solid and mostly complete methods section for this level, but it lacks enough procedural specificity to reach the higher range.
results_feedback: The results section is mostly correct, complete, and coherent, and it is clearly tied to the stated design. It reports descriptive statistics by condition and time point, states that all participants were included, and presents the mixed ANOVA in a recognizable structure appropriate for the course. Assumption checks are mentioned, main effects and the interaction are reported with test statistics and effect sizes, and follow-up post-hoc comparisons are used to interpret the interaction. The logic of the findings is clear and easy to follow. A notable strength is that the section reports the key pattern relevant to the hypothesis at both post-treatment and follow-up. The main limitations are at the level of completeness relative to the course sample and expected formatting. There is no separate demographics table, which the writing guide/sample expectations emphasize. The descriptive table is somewhat awkwardly formatted and contains standard errors that are not especially needed, while missing a cleaner presentation of participant characteristics. Assumption reporting is also somewhat generic; the section says assumptions were met but does not provide the tests or values behind that claim. In addition, the outlier discussion is somewhat inconsistent in tone and could be more formally reported. Still, for this course level, the analysis and reporting are clearly above adequate and close to the sample structure, which supports a good grade.
discussion_feedback: The discussion gives a clear main conclusion, answers the research question, and states that the hypothesis was supported for post-treatment outcomes. It also meaningfully addresses the follow-up finding that self-guided VRET improved further over time, which is important because this was the most surprising result pattern. The section relates the findings back to earlier literature, especially the established effectiveness of VRET and the Zainal et al. study on self-guided VRET. It also includes several relevant, study-specific limitations rather than only generic ones. In particular, the discussion of context differences between conditions and possible response bias from immediate post-treatment measurement in the therapist setting is thoughtful and directly tied to the observed findings. Future research suggestions generally follow from these limitations. The main weaknesses are that theoretical integration remains somewhat limited and the reasoning is not always fully developed. The explanation using self-efficacy is interesting, but it is introduced somewhat late and was not clearly prepared in the introduction, so the theory-discussion link is weaker than it could be. The discussion also does not engage very deeply with whether the study truly isolates therapist presence, given that multiple procedural differences between conditions existed. Broader practical implications are present but somewhat brief. Overall, this is a good discussion with relevant interpretation and criticism, though not fully comprehensive or tightly theory-driven enough for a higher score.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally readable, clearly structured, and understandable throughout. The sectioning is logical, and most paragraphs have a clear focus. Scientific language is mostly appropriate for this level, and the argument can be followed without major difficulty. However, there are quite a few language and formatting issues that keep the style from the higher range. There are repeated grammar and phrasing problems (e.g., article use, awkward sentence constructions, spacing and punctuation inconsistencies), and several compound terms are inconsistently written, such as 'selfguided', 'therapist-guided', and 'therapistguided'. APA style is also somewhat inconsistent, with citation formatting issues, occasional awkward referencing, and noticeable errors in the reference list. There are also some small wording inaccuracies and redundancies. These problems do not seriously impede understanding, but they are frequent enough that the language and style should be judged as adequate-to-good rather than polished.

intro_feedback: The introduction clearly states the research question implicitly and the hypothesis explicitly, addresses societal relevance early, defines SAD and core treatment concepts, and includes the three required core studies plus one self-found study (Zainal et al., 2021). The general line of reasoning is broadly logical: SAD is prevalent and impairing, VRET is promising, therapist involvement may be a barrier, and self-guided VRET therefore becomes a relevant comparison. This is enough for Tier 2. The paper also includes a basic theoretical framework via exposure/extinction and the role of therapist support, and prior studies are not merely listed but linked to the current comparison. However, it does not fully reach Tier 3. The reasoning is adequate rather than convincingly tight throughout, the theory is somewhat thin and not strongly integrated into the hypothesis, and the design justification relative to prior research gaps is present but not deeply argued. Some literature details are inaccurate relative to the course materials (e.g., years for Kampmann/Bouchard), and the transitions between studies are serviceable rather than strong building-block argumentation. Overall, this is a solid, above-average introduction but not yet a consistently strong one.
methods_feedback: The Methods section is coherent with the stated RQ and hypotheses and clearly describes a two-condition repeated-measures design. Participants are sufficiently described with sample size, mean age, SD, gender distribution, recruitment source, inclusion/exclusion criteria, random assignment, and compensation. Materials include a description of the VR setup and the main dependent measure, with reference, number of items, response scale, score range, interpretation, and a sample of item content. Procedure is chronological and understandable from assignment through follow-up. This clearly meets Tier 2. It does not fully reach Tier 3 because some required details are still not fully complete or optimally placed. For example, the intervention descriptions are understandable but not detailed enough to make all condition differences fully unambiguous or easily replicable; cut-off scores are not included where relevant; some procedural and materials information are somewhat mixed; and there is limited justification for several design choices. Still, for this course level the section is complete enough and coherent enough to be assessed as adequate.
results_feedback: The Results section reports the correct analysis for the design (mixed ANOVA), includes descriptive statistics at the operational level, reports main effects and the interaction with test statistics and p-values, includes effect sizes, discusses outliers and assumptions, and reports post-hoc comparisons with a correction method. This meets Tier 2 comfortably and largely reaches Tier 3. The reporting is coherent with the stated design, and the interpretation of the interaction is clear. However, it does not fully reach Tier 4 because the section is not as complete or polished as the sample results template: the demographic information per condition is not presented in its own table, there is only one table rather than the fuller expected set, and no graph is included even though the rubric expects one at Tier 2 and above. Because the statistical reporting itself is fairly strong and understandable for this level, I place it at the lower end of Tier 3 rather than Tier 2. In short: strong analysis reporting, but somewhat incomplete presentation.
discussion_feedback: The discussion clearly revisits the aim and answers the research question. It addresses the hypothesis, interprets the main findings at the construct level, and meaningfully discusses the notable pattern that self-guided VRET continued improving by follow-up. The paper compares the findings to prior studies from the introduction and explains what this study adds relative to the earlier VRET literature. It also includes several study-specific limitations, links them to possible effects on the conclusions, and offers concrete future research suggestions. This satisfies Tier 2 and largely meets Tier 3. The section is particularly stronger than average in identifying plausible confounds, such as context differences in questionnaire completion and treatment setting differences. It falls short of a higher Tier 3 or Tier 4 because the theoretical framework is only lightly evaluated, alternative interpretations are touched on but not systematically weighed, and the broader societal implications are somewhat brief and less fully tied back to the opening societal relevance than they could be. Overall, this is a good discussion with clear reasoning and relevant critical reflection.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally clear and readable, with a coherent overall structure and mostly focused paragraphs. Scientific language is used appropriately throughout, and grammar/spelling problems are present but not frequent enough to obstruct meaning. APA usage is mixed: many references and citations are recognizable and mostly functional, but there are multiple formatting inconsistencies, punctuation issues, spacing problems, and some citation/reference irregularities. There are also wording issues and awkward phrases in several places (e.g., article transitions, treatment descriptions, and minor sentence-level errors), so the writing is not yet near-faultless. This places the paper in Tier 2 rather than Tier 3. It is clearly understandable and adequately structured, but not polished enough for the 'good' language/style range.

intro_feedback: The introduction clearly presents a research question and a directional hypothesis, addresses societal relevance early, and includes the three core VRET articles plus a relevant self-found article on self-guided VRET. The overall line of reasoning is broadly coherent: SAD is important, exposure-based treatments are relevant, VRET is promising, and therapist involvement may still be a barrier. The paper also makes a reasonable attempt to connect prior studies to the present comparison rather than only listing them. This supports an Adequate range grade. However, the theoretical framework is only partly developed. The Pavlovian extinction account is mentioned, but it is not strongly integrated with the later argument about why therapist-guided VRET should outperform self-guided VRET; that expectation relies more on plausible reasoning than on a clearly elaborated theory linking variables. Scientific relevance is argued, but the design is not yet explicitly justified in much detail in relation to prior research gaps beyond stating that no direct comparison exists. Because the argument is relevant and mostly logical but not fully convincing or tightly theory-driven throughout, the introduction fits Tier 2 better than Tier 3.
methods_feedback: The methods section is clearly structured into participants, materials, and procedure, and the design is coherent with the stated RQ and hypothesis. Participants are described with sample size, age, SD, gender distribution, inclusion and exclusion criteria, random assignment, and compensation. Materials include a reasonably clear description of the two intervention conditions and a detailed description of the LSAS-SR with reference, item count, scale, sample items, score range, and interpretation; reliability/validity is also briefly mentioned. The procedure gives a chronological account from assignment through sessions to follow-up and debriefing. These features satisfy Tier 2 well. The section does not quite reach Tier 3 because some information placement and completeness are not fully optimal. There is no separate analyses subsection, some procedural details still blur into materials, and the description of standardization between conditions remains somewhat limited despite the conditions differing on more than therapist presence alone (e.g., home vs office context, different instruction formats). Also, the substantiation for exclusion criteria and some design choices is limited. Overall, this is a solid, above-passing methods section for this level, but not detailed enough for a clear Tier 3 score.
results_feedback: The results section is strong for this level and broadly follows the expected structure. The correct mixed ANOVA is reported for the design, key descriptive statistics are presented, main effects and the interaction are reported with F values, degrees of freedom, p values, and effect sizes, and post-hoc comparisons with Bonferroni correction are included. Outliers are discussed and a decision is made to retain them, and assumption checks are reported. This places the section in Tier 3. It does not score higher because some expected elements from the sample are missing or underdeveloped: there is no separate demographic table per condition, no graph of the score changes across conditions is included in the paper text provided, and the assumption reporting is fairly general rather than complete and specific. The outlier rationale is also somewhat thin, and the opening statement that there was 'no attrition or invalid data' sits awkwardly with the later report of multiple outliers. Still, the statistical reporting is coherent, understandable, and clearly above average for this assignment.
discussion_feedback: The discussion revisits the aim and hypothesis, states a clear main conclusion, and interprets the main findings at the construct level. It compares the findings to prior research from the introduction, explains how the current study adds to the literature, and discusses an unexpected pattern: the continued improvement in the self-guided condition at follow-up. It also includes multiple study-specific limitations and concrete future research directions. This supports a Tier 3 grade. The discussion is not fully at the excellent level because the integration with theory remains somewhat limited. The theoretical framework from the introduction is not explicitly evaluated in a deep way; instead, a new explanation based on self-efficacy is introduced rather late and not strongly tied back to the earlier framework. Some interpretations are plausible but somewhat speculative, and alternative explanations are not always systematically weighed. Still, the discussion is coherent, appropriately critical for this level, and meaningfully linked to both prior literature and practical implications, especially around accessibility of treatment.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally understandable and uses mostly appropriate scientific language. The section structure is clear, and most paragraphs have a discernible focus. Referencing is present throughout and mostly functional. This supports a Tier 2 score. However, there are enough language and APA-style issues to keep the grade in the lower part of that tier: repeated spacing/punctuation problems, inconsistent hyphenation and capitalization (e.g., selfguided/Selfguided, therapist-guided/Therapistguided), some awkward phrasing, occasional grammar errors, and several citation/reference inconsistencies. There are also small inaccuracies in article years relative to the required studies and some formatting issues in the results table and headings. These issues do not seriously obscure meaning, but they do reduce polish and consistency.

intro_feedback: The introduction clearly states a research question and hypothesis, addresses societal relevance early, and includes the 3 core studies plus an additional relevant study (Zainal et al., 2021). The overall line of reasoning is present and broadly logical: SAD is important, VRET is promising, therapist involvement may be a barrier, and self-guided VRET is therefore worth comparing to therapist-guided VRET. Key concepts are minimally defined, and scientific relevance is argued rather than only mentioned. The paper also includes a basic theoretical framework through exposure/extinction and the role of therapist support. This places the introduction solidly in Tier 2. It does not fully reach Tier 3 because the literature is still used somewhat study-by-study rather than consistently as tightly integrated building blocks, the theoretical framework is fairly limited and not strongly used to derive the full hypothesis, and the design choice is only somewhat explicitly justified in relation to prior research gaps. There is a clear gap, but the argumentation is not fully convincing throughout. Overall: adequate to somewhat above average introduction.
methods_feedback: The Methods section is coherent with the stated RQ and hypotheses and includes Participants, Materials, and Procedure. Participant information is fairly complete: sample size, mean age, SD, gender distribution, exclusion criteria, random assignment, and compensation are all reported. Materials include the intervention conditions and the LSAS-SR with reference, number of items, scale, example items, score range, and brief psychometric information. The procedure is chronological and mostly complete from assignment through follow-up and debriefing. This satisfies Tier 2 well. It does not fully reach Tier 3 because some details remain underdeveloped or slightly ambiguous for replication: the intervention protocols are described only moderately precisely, condition standardization is not fully specified, some information could be more clearly separated between Materials and Procedure, and not all design choices are explicitly justified. Still, for this course level, the section is clearly adequate and reasonably complete.
results_feedback: The Results section matches the expected design and uses an appropriate mixed ANOVA. Main effects and the interaction are reported with test statistics, p-values, and effect sizes. Descriptive statistics are presented at the operational level, and a table with means and SDs across conditions and time points is included. Outlier checks, assumption checks, and Bonferroni-corrected post-hoc tests are also reported. This clearly exceeds Tier 2 core criteria. I placed it at the lower end of Tier 3 because the reporting is generally coherent and quite close to the sample in structure, but it still falls short of a stronger Tier 3 score: the demographics table per condition is missing, there is no graph of score changes across conditions, and the assumption checks are reported rather generally rather than fully/completely. So the section is good overall, but not fully complete relative to the rubric and sample expectations.
discussion_feedback: The discussion clearly revisits the aim and hypothesis, states the main conclusion, and interprets the main findings at the construct level. It compares the findings to prior literature and discusses an unexpected finding: the continued improvement in the self-guided condition at follow-up. The student also revisits the theoretical side through therapist support and self-efficacy, and gives several study-specific limitations with related future directions. Practical relevance is addressed, especially around accessibility and treatment barriers. This places the discussion in Tier 2. It does not fully reach Tier 3 because the reasoning is not consistently deep or fully integrated: comparisons with prior research are somewhat brief, the theoretical framework is revisited only modestly rather than explicitly evaluated in terms of support/challenge/refinement, and alternative interpretations are only partly considered. The limitations are relevant and specific, but their implications for the strength of the conclusions could be analyzed more critically. Overall, a solid and adequate discussion.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally understandable throughout and has a clear overall structure with recognizable sections and mostly focused paragraphs. Scientific language is used appropriately for the most part. However, there are quite a few language and style issues that keep this from a higher score: awkward phrasing, inconsistent hyphenation/spelling of key terms (e.g., self-guided/selfguided, therapist-guided/therapistguided), several grammar and punctuation errors, some informal or imprecise wording, and a noticeable number of APA/reference inaccuracies. Paragraphing is mostly functional, but topical sentences and transitions are not consistently strong. This fits Tier 2 at the lower end: adequate readability and structure, but not polished.

intro_feedback: De introductie is duidelijk bovengemiddeld voor dit cursusniveau. De maatschappelijke relevantie wordt vroeg en concreet uitgewerkt, met aandacht voor prevalentie, impact op functioneren en problemen in de toegankelijkheid van zorg. Daarna volgt een logisch theoretisch kader rond vermijding, exposure, inhibitory learning en expectancy violation, dat goed aansluit op de onderzoeksvraag. De verplichte kernstudies (Anderson, Kampmann, Bouchard) worden op relevante wijze besproken en er wordt ook een extra studie gebruikt om het specifieke focuspunt van zelfgeleide VRET te onderbouwen. Sterk is dat de student niet alleen samenvat, maar ook expliciet toewerkt naar de lacune: de rol van begeleiding binnen VRET. De onderzoeksvraag en hypothesen zijn helder en passend bij de besproken literatuur. Wat de score iets onder een nog hoger niveau houdt, is dat de synthese tussen sommige theoretische onderdelen nog wat uitgebreider en scherper had gekund; bijvoorbeeld de koppeling tussen autonomie/self-determination theory en de concrete verwachtingen over verschillen tussen condities blijft enigszins speculatief. Ook zijn enkele bronnen voor maatschappelijke relevantie minder sterk wetenschappelijk dan ideaal. Toch is de redenering coherent, overtuigend en goed afgestemd op het onderzoeksontwerp.
methods_feedback: De methode is over het algemeen coherent en passend bij de onderzoeksvraag en hypothesen. De steekproef, werving en de meeste inclusie- en exclusiecriteria worden genoemd, en de randomisatieprocedure wordt beschreven. Ook de drie interventiecondities worden inhoudelijk voldoende onderscheiden voor dit niveau, en het is positief dat de student probeert te standaardiseren over sessieduur, aantal sessies en opbouw. De gebruikte afhankelijke maat (LSAS-SR) wordt in grote lijnen adequaat beschreven met aantal items, schaal en scorebereik. Tegelijkertijd mist de sectie een aantal elementen die volgens de schrijfwijzer wel verwacht worden. Zo ontbreken demografische kenmerken van de uiteindelijke steekproef zoals gemiddelde leeftijd, standaarddeviatie en genderverdeling, evenals informatie over eventuele beloning/compensatie. De beschrijving van de interventies is redelijk, maar nog niet helemaal precies genoeg om de studie goed te kunnen repliceren; bijvoorbeeld de concrete invulling van de exposure-opbouw en de inhoudelijke standaardisatie tussen condities blijven vrij globaal. Ook staat designinformatie deels in de procedure in plaats van puur in een analysesubsectie, en een aparte beschrijving van de geplande analyse ontbreekt. Daarmee is de methode adequaat tot goed, maar niet volledig.
results_feedback: De resultatensectie volgt redelijk goed de verwachte structuur voor dit vak. Er is een tabel met gemiddelden en standaarddeviaties per conditie en meetmoment, de gebruikte analyse sluit aan op het design, en de belangrijkste effecten worden duidelijk en correct gerapporteerd. Ook de assumptiecontroles worden benoemd op een passend detailniveau voor tweedejaarsstudenten. De interpretatie van de uitkomsten blijft dicht bij het operationele niveau: er is een significant tijdseffect, geen conditie-effect en geen interactie, gevolgd door post-hocvergelijkingen. Dat maakt de sectie coherent en goed leesbaar. Wat voorkomt dat de score hoger uitvalt, is dat de rapportage niet volledig het voorbeeldniveau haalt: er ontbreekt een demografische tabel, de figuur wordt wel genoemd maar niet daadwerkelijk uitgewerkt in de ingeleverde tekst, en de post-hocrapportage had iets preciezer gekund. Daarnaast roept de gerapporteerde effectgrootte bij het tijdseffect enige vragen op in verhouding tot de zeer hoge F-waarde, maar dit is niet zo problematisch dat het de sectie sterk verlaagt. Al met al een solide, bovengemiddelde resultatensectie voor dit niveau.
discussion_feedback: De discussie is inhoudelijk sterk genoeg en sluit goed aan op de resultaten. De student opent met een duidelijke hoofdconclusie, beantwoordt de onderzoeksvraag expliciet en maakt helder dat de hypothese over sterkere effecten van begeleide interventies niet is bevestigd. Daarna worden de bevindingen op logische wijze gekoppeld aan eerder onderzoek en aan het theoretisch kader van inhibitory learning en expectancy violation. Positief is dat de student echt probeert te verklaren waarom zelfgeleide VRET vergelijkbare effecten liet zien, en daarbij meerdere alternatieve interpretaties bespreekt, zoals de mate van standaardisatie en de gevoeligheid van de uitkomstmaat. Ook bevat de discussie relevante beperkingen en concrete suggesties voor vervolgonderzoek. De bredere implicatie, namelijk dat zelfgeleide VRET mogelijk een toegankelijk alternatief vormt, volgt redelijk uit de bevindingen en wordt niet volledig overspeeld. Wat de score iets drukt, is dat de discussie soms wat herhalend is, inclusief een letterlijk dubbele zin aan het begin. Daarnaast had de terugkoppeling naar theorie nog kritischer gekund: de student suggereert steun voor theoretische aannames, maar werkt minder uit welke theoretische onderdelen nu daadwerkelijk getest zijn en welke niet. Ook blijven de praktische implicaties nog tamelijk algemeen. Desondanks is de redenering coherent en overtuigend voor dit cursusniveau.
lang_style_feedback: De tekst is over het algemeen helder, goed leesbaar en passend wetenschappelijk geformuleerd. De opbouw van de paper is logisch en de meeste paragrafen hebben een duidelijke focus. De student gebruikt signaalwoorden en overgangen meestal effectief, waardoor de algemene lijn van het betoog goed te volgen is. Het taalniveau is voor deze opdracht bovengemiddeld. Er zijn wel enkele stilistische en APA-technische onvolkomenheden. Zo staan er kleine inconsistenties in interpunctie en spatiëring, bevat de discussie een duidelijke herhaling van een zin, en zijn er enkele slordigheden in de referentielijst en bronvermelding. Ook is de lay-out van de resultatentabel en figuurverwijzing niet helemaal netjes uitgewerkt. Deze punten belemmeren het begrip niet sterk, maar maken wel dat de stijl niet op een bijna foutloos niveau zit. Daarom past een goede, maar geen uitstekende score.

intro_feedback: De introductie heeft een duidelijke en logische opbouw van maatschappelijke relevantie naar theoretisch kader, eerdere literatuur en uiteindelijk de onderzoeksvraag en hypothesen. De maatschappelijke relevantie van sociale angststoornis wordt overtuigend geschetst, en de koppeling met toegankelijkheid van behandeling en de mogelijke waarde van zelfgeleide VRET is helder. Ook het theoretisch kader is sterker dan gemiddeld: vermijding, inhibitory learning, expectancy violation en de mogelijke rol van autonomie/begeleiding worden goed verbonden aan de onderzoeksvraag. De drie verplichte studies worden besproken en er is een extra relevante studie opgenomen over zelfgeleide VRET. De onderzoeksvraag en hypothesen zijn duidelijk geformuleerd en sluiten aan op het voorgaande. Wel blijft de literatuurverwerking soms meer beschrijvend dan echt synthetiserend, en sommige theoretische claims over autonomie en begeleiding zijn nog wat speculatief of minder direct empirisch onderbouwd. Ook had de overgang van theorie naar concrete ontwerpkeuzes nog iets explicieter gekund. Desondanks is de redenering coherent en overtuigend voor dit niveau.
methods_feedback: De methode is in grote lijnen coherent en passend bij de onderzoeksvraag: de drie condities sluiten aan op de hypothesen en het design wordt uiteindelijk duidelijk benoemd. De participantenparagraaf bevat relevante inclusie- en exclusiecriteria en een geplande steekproefgrootte per conditie. Ook de randomisatie wordt genoemd. Positief is dat de interventies inhoudelijk op elkaar worden afgestemd en dat standaardisatie wordt benoemd om confounds te beperken. Tegelijkertijd mist de sectie meerdere elementen die volgens de schrijfwijzer eigenlijk explicieter en vollediger moeten worden uitgewerkt. Zo ontbreken concrete demografische gegevens van de uiteindelijke steekproef (gemiddelde leeftijd, SD, genderverdeling), compensatie/reward wordt niet genoemd, en de operationalisatie van diagnose-instelling blijft vaag. Bij de materialen is de LSAS-SR redelijk beschreven, maar de bronvermelding is niet ideaal en details zoals een voorbeelditem of psychometrische onderbouwing ontbreken. De procedure is vrij summier en bevat nog ontwerpinformatie die beter in een aparte design/analysis-beschrijving had gepast. De analysemethode wordt pas in de resultaten volledig duidelijk. Al met al is de methode begrijpelijk en grotendeels correct, maar niet volledig genoeg voor een hogere score.
results_feedback: De resultaten zijn over het algemeen duidelijk, relevant en passend bij het beschreven design. Er wordt een passende mixed ANOVA gerapporteerd, assumpties worden gecontroleerd, en de hoofdeffecten en interactie worden helder weergegeven. Ook wordt een tabel met gemiddelde scores per conditie en meetmoment gegeven, en de interpretatie van de uitkomsten is correct: alle groepen verbeteren, zonder verschil tussen interventies. Dat sluit goed aan op de onderzoeksvraag. Vergeleken met het voorbeeldresultatenbestand is deze sectie echter wat minder volledig uitgewerkt. Er ontbreekt een aparte demografische tabel van de steekproef, en de rapportage van descriptieve statistiek is beperkt tot de uitkomstmaat. De vermelding van figuur 1 is aanwezig, maar de figuur zelf is niet echt uitgewerkt in de aangeleverde tekst. Ook blijven sommige details van de post-hocvergelijkingen en de operationele rapportage wat summier. De statistische rapportage is dus grotendeels correct en coherent, maar niet zo volledig of voorbeeldgetrouw als nodig voor een hogere beoordeling.
discussion_feedback: De discussie is sterk voor dit niveau. De sectie opent met een duidelijke hoofdconclusie die de onderzoeksvraag beantwoordt en expliciet aangeeft welke hypothese wel en niet werd ondersteund. Vervolgens worden de bevindingen goed gekoppeld aan eerdere literatuur en aan het inhibitory learning-kader. Vooral sterk is dat de afwezigheid van verschillen tussen de condities niet wordt genegeerd, maar inhoudelijk wordt geïnterpreteerd met meerdere plausibele verklaringen, zoals standaardisatie van de zelfgeleide conditie en mogelijke beperkingen van de gebruikte uitkomstmaat. Ook de terugkoppeling naar de theorie is aanwezig en functioneel. Verder bevat de discussie relevante en studie-specifieke beperkingen, zoals het ontbreken van follow-upmetingen, beperkte generaliseerbaarheid en het niet meten van procesvariabelen. De voorstellen voor vervolgonderzoek volgen logisch uit deze beperkingen. Een klein minpunt is dat er enige herhaling voorkomt aan het begin van de sectie en dat de praktische implicaties nog iets concreter uitgewerkt hadden kunnen worden. Toch is de redenering coherent, volledig en overtuigend voor een tweedejaars paper.
lang_style_feedback: De tekst is over het geheel genomen helder, goed leesbaar en passend wetenschappelijk geformuleerd. De opbouw van de secties is logisch en de meeste alinea’s hebben een duidelijke focus. De stijl is overwegend correct en begrijpelijk, met voldoende signposting en samenhang. Er zijn wel enkele taal- en stijlfouten en wat onzorgvuldigheden die de kwaliteit iets drukken, zoals herhaling van zinnen in de discussie, kleine inconsistenties in terminologie (bijvoorbeeld iVET/exposure in vivo), enkele APA-onvolkomenheden in de literatuurlijst en referenties, en soms wat lange of omslachtige zinnen. Ook is de lay-out van de resultatentabel wat rommelig in de aangeleverde tekst. Deze punten belemmeren het begrip niet sterk, maar maken de tekst minder strak dan bij een hogere score.

intro_feedback: The introduction shows a clear and coherent line of reasoning from societal relevance to theory, prior research, and the research question. The societal relevance is strong and well connected to the treatment gap in mental health care. Key concepts such as avoidance, inhibitory learning, expectancy violation, and presence are explained clearly and mostly linked well to the proposed comparison between self-guided VRET, therapist-guided VRET, and in vivo exposure. The paper also uses the required core studies appropriately and adds a relevant extra study on self-guided VRET. The research question and hypotheses are explicit and logically follow from the preceding argument. Strong points are the generally good synthesis of theory and literature and the convincing motivation for examining guidance within VRET. A limitation is that some parts remain slightly more descriptive than fully integrative, especially in the literature review, and the theoretical argument for why therapist guidance should outperform self-guided VRET could have been sharpened further. There are also a few references included in the reference list that are not clearly used in the argument, and the exact design rationale could have been stated a bit more concisely at the transition to the method. Overall, this is a good to strong introduction for this course level.
methods_feedback: The method is coherent and clearly aligned with the stated research question and hypotheses. The design is appropriate for comparing three intervention conditions over time, and the participant section includes recruitment, inclusion and exclusion criteria, and planned sample size. Random allocation is mentioned, and the dependent variable is clearly identified. The materials section describes the main questionnaire reasonably well, including number of items, response scale, and score range. The intervention descriptions are understandable and the effort to standardize the conditions is explained, which supports internal validity. However, the methods are not fully complete at the level expected for a higher grade. Important participant details such as mean age, age SD, gender distribution, and compensation/reward are missing, even though these are explicitly expected in the guide. intro_feedback: De introductie voldoet duidelijk aan Tier 3. De onderzoeksvraag is helder, relevant en goed gekoppeld aan zowel maatschappelijke als wetenschappelijke relevantie. results_feedback: De resultatensectie zit in Tier 2. discussion_feedback: De discussie is inhoudelijk sterk en haalt Tier 3. results_feedback: The results section meets Tier 2. discussion_feedback: The discussion clearly reaches Tier 3. The main conclusion is explicit, the RQ is revisited, and the hypothesis is directly addressed and partly rejected. intro_feedback: The introduction is clearly above average for this course level. The use of the LSAS-SR is appropriate and mostly described at the expected level. However, several elements that the writing guide expects are missing or underdeveloped. The theoretical implications are relatively brief and do not fully return to the introduction's theories in a systematic way. Overall, the discussion is relevant and mostly coherent, but it is not consistently convincing or tightly grounded enough for a higher grade.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally readable and uses mostly appropriate scientific language. The overall structure is clear, with recognizable sections and a logical order.
