Inclusion/exclusion criteria are also not always clearly or convincingly justified, and a few phrases are confusing (e.g., diagnosis and medication timing criteria). So this is an adequate but not strongly detailed methods section.
results_feedback: The results section is relatively strong and follows the sample structure reasonably closely. The correct overall analysis is reported for the design: a 3 x 2 mixed ANOVA. The student reports main effects, the interaction, descriptive statistics, assumption checks, an outlier check, post-hoc comparisons with Holm correction, effect sizes in parts of the output, demographic information by condition, and refers to a figure. This clearly exceeds Tier 1 and satisfies Tier 2 well. It also largely meets Tier 3: assumption checks are addressed, post-hoc tests are presented and interpreted, and the reporting is coherent with the stated design. The main limitation is that the presentation is somewhat messy and appears partly copied from software output rather than fully adapted into polished narrative/tables. The demographics table is incomplete relative to the guide because mean age and SD per condition are not clearly presented in a clean table, and some tables are not ideally formatted or labelled. There is also minor inconsistency in whether age was included as a factor/covariate, which should have been explained better. Still, compared with the course expectations and sample, this is a good results section.
discussion_feedback: The discussion is a good section overall. It clearly restates the aim, revisits the hypothesis, answers the research question, and interprets the findings at the construct level. The student distinguishes expected from unexpected findings and offers an explanation for why group VR did not outperform individual VR. The findings are linked back to theory, especially inhibitory learning/expectancy violation, and to prior literature such as Kampmann and Anderson. The discussion also includes multiple study-specific limitations and corresponding future research directions, and it returns to broader societal relevance near the end. This is stronger than Tier 2 and fits Tier 3 overall. It does not fully reach Tier 4 because the discussion still reads somewhat like a sequence of required elements rather than one fully seamless argument. Some explanations are plausible but not deeply evaluated against alternatives, and the treatment of the theoretical framework is competent rather than especially critical or refined. Still, the reasoning is coherent, limitations are connected to interpretation, and implications are appropriately cautious for this level.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally understandable and uses scientific language consistently enough to pass comfortably. Section structure is clear, and most paragraphs have a discernible focus. Referencing is present throughout. This supports a Tier 2 grade. However, the writing is not strong enough for Tier 3 because grammar, phrasing, punctuation, and APA issues are too frequent. There are many awkward or incorrect formulations, some run-on or clumsy sentences, spacing/punctuation problems, inconsistent terminology, and several reference issues. Some examples include informal wording, odd transitions, typographical mistakes, and citation/reference inaccuracies. The title page details are also clearly unrealistic or erroneous, though these do not affect content. Overall, the paper is readable and structured, but language and APA are only adequate rather than polished.

intro_feedback: The introduction clearly contains a research question/hypothesis, addresses societal relevance, defines key concepts, and includes the 3 required core articles plus an additional self-found article. The paper also presents a theoretical framework around maladaptive cognitions, safety behaviors, avoidance, and inhibitory learning, and this framework is linked to the expectation that group VR might outperform individual VR. Prior studies are not merely listed; there is a visible attempt to connect them as a progression toward the present study. This meets Tier 2 well. However, the argument is not consistently tight enough for Tier 3. Some study descriptions are inaccurate or confusing relative to the cited articles, the ordering/building-block logic is only partly convincing, and the main hypothesis is phrased somewhat unclearly ('The main hypothesis is whether...'). The design justification is present but not very explicit or fully precise. Overall, this is an adequate-to-good introduction with a clear line of reasoning, but not a fully convincing seamless argument.
methods_feedback: The Methods section is broadly coherent with the stated RQ and hypotheses and includes Participants, Materials, and Procedure. Sample size, mean age with SD, age range, gender proportions, inclusion/exclusion criteria, random assignment, and compensation are reported. The LSAS-SR is described with reference, item count, scale, scoring range, and interpretation, and the intervention conditions are described in understandable detail. This satisfies Tier 2 core criteria. It does not fully reach Tier 3 because some information is incomplete or imprecise: participant reporting is awkwardly phrased, inclusion/exclusion criteria are not always clearly justified, the questionnaire description lacks a proper sample item formulation and stronger measurement detail, and information is not always presented in the ideal subsection. Standardization is mentioned, but confound control and rationale for design choices are only lightly developed. Overall, the section is adequately detailed for this course level, but not fully polished.
results_feedback: The Results section is stronger and closely follows the expected sample structure. The correct mixed ANOVA is used for the stated design, descriptive statistics are reported at the operational level, outliers are checked, assumptions are discussed, main effects and the interaction are reported with test statistics and p-values, post-hoc tests with Holm correction are included, and a figure is referenced. Demographic information is also presented in table form. This clearly meets Tier 2 and approaches Tier 3. I placed it at 7.5 because the overall structure is strong and the reporting is mostly coherent with the sample style, and effect sizes are included for several analyses. It does not go higher because table formatting is messy/inconsistent, the demographic table omits the requested age information per condition, and there are some reporting oddities (e.g., unnecessary age covariate appearing in ANOVA tables without prior explanation, some awkward phrasing, and incomplete figure presentation in the text provided). Still, for this level, the section is good and above average.
discussion_feedback: The discussion clearly revisits the aim and hypothesis, states that the first part of the hypothesis was supported and the second was not, and interprets the findings at the construct level. It compares the results to prior research, especially Kampmann et al. and Anderson et al., and proposes a plausible explanation for the unexpected finding that group VR did not outperform individual VR. The theoretical framework is explicitly revisited through inhibitory learning/expectancy violation, and limitations are study-specific rather than generic. Future research suggestions follow logically from those limitations, and broader practical relevance is addressed at the end. This meets Tier 3 overall. I did not score it higher because some interpretations are somewhat repetitive or speculative, the connection back to the broader theory is good but not especially nuanced, and some limitation reasoning is not fully developed in terms of impact on conclusions. Still, the section is coherent, relevant, and clearly above average for this course level.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally understandable and uses scientific language throughout, with a recognizable academic structure. Most paragraphs have a clear focus, and the overall organization is workable. However, there are frequent language and style problems that keep this from the 'good' range: awkward phrasing, grammatical errors, punctuation issues, inconsistent wording, several APA/reference mistakes, and some imprecise or non-academic formulations. There are also obvious formatting problems in the title page details and some references. These issues do not usually obscure meaning, so the paper remains passable to adequate in style, but it is not polished. Therefore, a 6.5 fits best.

intro_feedback: De introductie is duidelijk boven gemiddeld voor dit niveau. Er is een heldere maatschappelijke relevantie, de onderzoeksvraag is expliciet en relevant, en de tekst bouwt in grote lijnen logisch op van probleemstelling naar theorie, eerdere literatuur, kennislacune en hypothese. Positief is ook dat de verplichte studies van Anderson, Kampmann en Bouchard daadwerkelijk worden besproken en gekoppeld aan het huidige ontwerp, plus een extra studie over adolescenten. De theoretische onderbouwing met Emotional Processing Theory en Inhibitory Learning Theory sluit goed aan bij exposure en de vergelijking tussen behandelvormen. Wel zijn er beperkingen in de argumentatie die maken dat dit nog niet richting een 8 of hoger gaat: sommige claims zijn te stellig of te weinig precies onderbouwd, de theoretische lijn is soms wat simplistisch uitgewerkt, en enkele literatuurinterpretaties zijn niet helemaal scherp of consistent. Ook is de overgang van theorie naar de specifieke verwachting over langetermijneffecten niet overal even overtuigend uitgewerkt. Toch is de line of reasoning duidelijk coherent en overtuigend genoeg voor een goede score.
methods_feedback: De methode is in de basis coherent en passend bij de onderzoeksvraag: er is een RCT-achtig design met twee condities en drie meetmomenten, wat goed aansluit op de hypothese over kortetermijn- en langetermijneffecten. De secties deelnemers, materialen en procedure zijn aanwezig, en belangrijke elementen zoals inclusie/exclusiecriteria, randomisatie en het meetinstrument worden genoemd. Tegelijkertijd mist de methode meerdere details die volgens de writing guide wel verwacht worden. De beschrijving van de behandelingen is vrij summier en laat belangrijke zaken open, zoals hoe de sessies precies zijn opgebouwd, hoe vergelijkbaarheid tussen condities is gewaarborgd, en hoe de exposure-opbouw concreet verliep. Bij de LSAS-CA is wel veel informatie gegeven, maar de beschrijving is niet helemaal strak en deels procedureel. De procedure is erg kort en bevat te weinig chronologische details om het onderzoek echt goed te kunnen reproduceren. Ook ontbreekt informatie over bijvoorbeeld beloning/compensatie in preciezere vorm, duur van afnames en verdere standaardisatie. Daarom is dit voldoende tot redelijk, maar niet echt sterk uitgewerkt.
results_feedback: De resultaten zijn net voldoende, vooral omdat de algemene analysekern wel aansluit op het design en er geprobeerd wordt de voorbeeldstructuur te volgen met descriptieve statistiek, ANOVA en post-hocvergelijkingen. Er staan echter duidelijke tekortkomingen in de rapportage die de kwaliteit behoorlijk drukken. De demografische tabel is onhandig vormgegeven en wijkt af van de verwachte presentatie; bovendien is zij inconsistent met de participantensectie, waar alleen jongens en meiden werden genoemd terwijl de tabel ook non-binaire deelnemers bevat. In de inferentiële statistiek ontbreken essentiële vrijheidsgraden in alle F-tests, waardoor de rapportage onvolledig is. Tabel 2 is ook duidelijk fout of beschadigd opgemaakt, waardoor de gemiddelden en standaarddeviaties moeilijk leesbaar zijn. Verder is er een inhoudelijke inconsistentie tussen methode, resultaten en discussie: in de resultaten wordt gesproken over een 'drie maanden follow-up', terwijl elders 12 maanden staat. Ook de interpretatie van de follow-upresultaten is niet overal even helder. Omdat de analyses in grote lijnen relevant zijn maar de rapportage onvolledig en deels inconsistent is, komt deze sectie uit op een minimale voldoende.
discussion_feedback: De discussie is degelijk en laat zien dat de student probeert de bevindingen echt te interpreteren in plaats van alleen te herhalen. De hoofdconclusie wordt helder geformuleerd, en er wordt onderscheid gemaakt tussen kortetermijn- en langetermijnbevindingen. Positief is ook dat onverwachte of minder gunstige patronen niet worden genegeerd, maar expliciet besproken. De student koppelt de resultaten terug aan eerdere studies en aan de twee theoretische kaders, en benoemt mogelijke verklaringen zoals ontwikkelingsverschillen bij adolescenten en beperkingen in generalisatie van VRET naar echte sociale situaties. Dat past goed bij de rubric. Tegelijkertijd zijn er enkele zwakkere punten. De interpretatie is soms niet helemaal consistent met de gerapporteerde resultaten, vooral rondom de langetermijnvergelijking tussen condities. Sommige claims zijn speculatief of te stellig geformuleerd gegeven het design. De kritische reflectie is aanwezig en relevant, maar deels wat generiek en niet altijd scherp gekoppeld aan de specifieke bevindingen. De implicaties voor praktijk en vervolgonderzoek zijn nuttig, maar soms wat uitgebreid en ambitieus ten opzichte van de sterkte van de data. Al met al is dit een goede, maar niet uitzonderlijk sterke discussie.
lang_style_feedback: De tekst is over het algemeen goed te volgen en heeft een herkenbare wetenschappelijke structuur. De meeste onderdelen en alinea's zijn logisch geordend, en de rode draad blijft meestal zichtbaar. Er zijn echter vrij veel taal- en stijlfouten die maken dat het geheel niet echt strak is uitgewerkt. Denk aan grammaticale onnauwkeurigheden, slordige formuleringen, inconsistent gebruik van termen en afkortingen, en APA-onregelmatigheden in zowel tekst als referentielijst. Ook zijn er meerdere typfouten en formattingproblemen, bijvoorbeeld in tabellen, interpunctie, spaties rond referenties en statistische notatie. Sommige zinnen zijn onnodig omslachtig of net niet precies. Dit belemmert het begrip niet ernstig, maar voorkomt wel een hogere score. Daarom past een licht bovenvoldoende beoordeling het best.

intro_feedback: The introduction shows a clear and generally coherent line of reasoning from societal relevance to theory, prior research, and the research question. The societal relevance is well established and linked to the target population of adolescents with social anxiety disorder. The student also includes relevant theory (Emotional Processing Theory and Inhibitory Learning Theory) and uses the required core studies (Anderson et al., Kampmann et al., Bouchard et al.) plus an additional adolescent-focused article. The research gap is clearly identified: evidence for the combined treatment in adolescents on the long term is lacking. The research question and hypothesis are explicit and relevant. Strong points are the clear hourglass structure and the attempt to connect theory to the expected superiority of VRET+CGT. Weaknesses are that parts of the theoretical reasoning are somewhat oversimplified or imprecise, some claims are stronger than the cited literature appears to support, and the literature review is still somewhat study-by-study rather than fully synthesized. There are also some inaccuracies and awkward formulations in interpreting prior findings. Overall, however, the introduction is solidly above average for this level and convincingly motivates the study.
methods_feedback: The method is coherent and broadly aligned with the research question and hypotheses. Participants, inclusion/exclusion criteria, recruitment, and randomization are described, which is a clear strength. The general design is also appropriate for the stated aim, and the main instrument is named and described in reasonable detail. However, the section is only somewhat comprehensible and not fully complete. Important procedural and replication details are missing or too vague, such as how randomization was performed, whether assessors were blinded, how treatment fidelity was ensured, what exactly happened in each session, and how the follow-up was conducted. The materials subsection mixes intervention description and measurement details somewhat inconsistently. The LSAS-CA description contains useful information, but the SCID-5 description belongs more clearly under participants/diagnostics and is not fully tailored to the study procedure. There are also inconsistencies in sample description: the participant section reports only boys and girls, but the results table later includes non-binary participants, which creates confusion. Overall, the study design is coherent and mostly correct, but the methods are not complete enough to reach a clearly good score.
results_feedback: The results section follows the expected overall structure and includes descriptive information, an ANOVA, and post-hoc comparisons, which is appropriate for the design. However, there are substantial reporting problems that lower the score. First, the demographic table is poorly formatted and inconsistent with the participant section: the results table includes non-binary participants, whereas the participant section reported only 33 girls and 27 boys. Second, Table 2 is badly formatted and difficult to interpret, making the descriptive statistics unclear. Third, crucial statistical information is incomplete: the F-tests are reported without degrees of freedom, which is a major omission at this level. The assumptions section is also too vague, with claims that all p-values were > .05 but without specific tests or values except Greenhouse-Geisser. In addition, the reporting of the follow-up interval is inconsistent: the method describes a 12-month follow-up, but the post-hoc text refers to a three-month follow-up. There are also formatting/statistical notation issues such as 'p = < .001'. The main pattern of findings is still understandable, and the analyses are relevant to the design, so this is not a failing section, but it is only just adequate because of the incompleteness and inconsistencies.
discussion_feedback: The discussion provides a clear main conclusion, answers the research question, and distinguishes between short-term and long-term findings. The student engages with expected and unexpected findings and relates them back to earlier literature, which is a strength. The discussion also attempts to connect the findings to the theoretical framework, especially Emotional Processing Theory and Inhibitory Learning Theory, and it offers several study-specific limitations and meaningful future research directions. The broader implications for clinical practice and society are also addressed. However, there are some issues that prevent a higher score. The interpretation is at times stronger than the reported data warrant, especially because the results section itself contains inconsistencies. Some reasoning is repetitive, and the third finding paragraph partly overlaps with the first conclusion rather than adding a genuinely distinct interpretive point. There are also moments where the student seems to overstate what can be concluded about durability and treatment superiority. Still, the discussion is coherent, relevant, and more than a simple repetition of the results, making it a solid adequate-to-good section.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally readable and the scientific tone is mostly appropriate for a second-year student paper. The overall structure is clear, and most sections and paragraphs have an identifiable focus. The argument is usually understandable. However, there are frequent language and style problems that limit clarity. These include grammar issues, awkward or literal phrasing, punctuation problems, inconsistent terminology (e.g., SAS/SAD, VRET+CGT/CGT+VRET), and many APA/reference formatting inconsistencies. There are also several sentence-level problems that make the writing less precise than it should be, and table formatting is weak. Still, the paper remains understandable throughout, so the language does not impede comprehension. This places the paper in the developing-to-adequate range, slightly below average for polish but acceptable overall.

intro_feedback: De introductie heeft een duidelijke en relevante onderzoeksvraag, een herkenbare maatschappelijke relevantie en een redelijke lijn van probleem naar theorie, eerdere studies en hypothese. Positief is dat de student de verplichte kernartikelen (Anderson, Kampmann, Bouchard) bespreekt, de adolescentenpopulatie expliciet motiveert en de keuze voor een follow-updesign verantwoordt. Ook is er een poging tot theoretische onderbouwing met Emotional Processing Theory en Inhibitory Learning Theory, gekoppeld aan de vergelijking tussen VRET+CGT en CGT+in vivo. Dat past goed bij de opdracht. Tegelijk blijft de argumentatie op meerdere punten slechts ‘goed genoeg’ in plaats van echt overtuigend. De theoriebespreking is deels simplificerend en soms niet helemaal scherp geformuleerd; uitspraken als dat VRET ‘vooral gedragsmatig werkt waardoor angst gedeeltelijk terug kan komen’ worden vrij stellig gebracht zonder sterke uitwerking. De literatuur wordt regelmatig meer samengevat dan echt synthetisch met elkaar verbonden. Er zitten ook enkele inhoudelijke onnauwkeurigheden of onduidelijkheden in de bespreking van studies en concepten. Desondanks is de rode draad duidelijk, de hypothese sluit aan op het voorafgaande, en de relevantie van de studie voor deze doelgroep komt overtuigend genoeg naar voren. Daarom boven gemiddeld, maar niet op excellent niveau.
methods_feedback: De methode is in grote lijnen coherent en passend bij de onderzoeksvraag: een gerandomiseerd design met twee behandelcondities en meerdere meetmomenten is logisch voor een vraag naar langetermijneffecten. De participantenparagraaf bevat belangrijke elementen zoals leeftijd, geslacht, diagnose, inclusie- en exclusiecriteria, werving en randomisatie. Ook worden de twee behandelcondities beschreven en is duidelijk dat alleen de vorm van exposure verschilt. Dat is een sterk punt. Toch mist de sectie meerdere details die volgens de schrijfgids verwacht worden. De procedure is erg beknopt en beschrijft onvoldoende chronologisch wat deelnemers precies doen van aanmelding tot debriefing. Er ontbreekt informatie over bijvoorbeeld duur en inhoud van afzonderlijke sessies in de procedure, wie welke metingen afnam, hoe follow-up precies verliep, en hoe therapietrouw of standaardisatie tussen therapeuten werd bewaakt. In de materialen staan bovendien procedurele elementen door elkaar met beschrijvingen van meetinstrumenten. De beschrijving van de LSAS-CA is redelijk volledig, maar voor de SCID-5 ontbreken formele bronvermelding en enkele operationalisatiedetails. Ook is niet helemaal helder hoe de afhankelijke variabele exact op alle meetmomenten werd afgenomen. Al met al is de methode voldoende en grotendeels correct, maar niet volledig uitgewerkt of echt gemakkelijk repliceerbaar.
results_feedback: De resultatensectie bevat de basiselementen die verwacht worden: er is een demografische tabel, een tabel met uitkomstscores, een mixed ANOVA, assumpties en post-hocvergelijkingen. Daarmee sluit de student aan bij de vereiste structuur. Toch zijn er duidelijke problemen in volledigheid, nauwkeurigheid en consistentie, waardoor dit net voldoende is. Het grootste probleem is de onvolledige statistische rapportage: bij alle F-toetsen ontbreken vrijheidsgraden, waardoor de kernrapportage niet correct is. Tabel 2 is bovendien slecht vormgegeven en moeilijk leesbaar; de gemiddelden en standaarddeviaties zijn niet helder per conditie en meetmoment gepresenteerd. Er zit ook een inhoudelijke inconsistentie in de tekst: in de methode is sprake van een 12-maanden follow-up, maar later wordt in de resultaten ook gesproken over een ‘drie maanden follow-up’. Daarnaast wordt gezegd dat de CGT+VRET-conditie groter afneemt, terwijl de gerapporteerde gemiddelden juist laten zien dat CGT+VRET op follow-up lager scoort dan CGT+in vivo, maar tussen post en follow-up stabiel blijft terwijl CGT+in vivo verder verbetert. Die interpretatie had preciezer gemoeten. De assumptierapportage blijft vrij oppervlakkig (‘p-waarden allemaal > .05’) en niet volgens het voorbeeldniveau. Omdat de gekozen analyse wel passend is bij het design en de hoofdlijn van de resultaten nog te volgen is, blijft dit op een krap voldoende niveau, maar duidelijk onder gemiddeld.
discussion_feedback: De discussie begint sterk met een duidelijke terugkoppeling naar doel, hypothese en belangrijkste bevindingen. De student onderscheidt ook netjes tussen korte- en langetermijneffecten en probeert onverwachte bevindingen inhoudelijk te interpreteren. Dat is belangrijk en gebeurt hier redelijk overtuigend. Positief is verder dat eerdere literatuur opnieuw wordt gebruikt, dat theorieën uit de introductie terugkomen en dat er meerdere concrete beperkingen en richtingen voor vervolgonderzoek worden genoemd. De discussie heeft dus zeker meer dan alleen een herhaling van de resultaten. Tegelijk zijn er ook zwakkere punten. De interpretatie is soms niet helemaal strak in lijn met de gerapporteerde resultaten, vooral doordat de beschrijving van het langetermijnpatroon op sommige punten verwarrend is. Ook worden enkele verklaringen vrij speculatief gepresenteerd, bijvoorbeeld over neurobiologische ontwikkeling en generalisatie, zonder heel zorgvuldig af te wegen hoe direct de huidige studie dat werkelijk testte. De kritische reflectie is relevant, maar had nog sterker gekund door meer studiespecifieke beperkingen te bespreken, zoals steekproefomvang, mogelijke powerproblemen, therapist effects, of de consequenties van de wat beperkte meet- en analysekaders. De slotimplicaties zijn relevant, maar soms iets stelliger dan de resultaten volledig rechtvaardigen. Daarom is dit een degelijke, bovengemiddelde discussie, maar niet helemaal consistent of diep genoeg voor een hogere score.
lang_style_feedback: De tekst is over het algemeen goed leesbaar en de globale structuur is duidelijk: inleiding, methode, resultaten, discussie en referenties zijn aanwezig en logisch geordend. De student gebruikt meestal wetenschappelijke taal en de rode draad blijft voor de lezer goed te volgen. Tegelijk zijn er vrij veel kleinere taal- en stijlfouten die de kwaliteit drukken. Er komen grammaticale fouten, slordige formuleringen, inconsequente terminologie en typografische problemen voor. Voorbeelden zijn foutieve spaties of interpunctie bij referenties, wisselend gebruik van SAS/SAD, Engels en Nederlands door elkaar, en zinnen die stilistisch stroef of ongrammaticaal zijn. Ook APA is niet consequent: meerdere referenties bevatten formattingfouten, onvolledigheden of afwijkende notatie, en in de tekst zijn sommige bronverwijzingen en statistische notaties niet netjes volgens APA. Daarnaast zijn sommige tabellen onduidelijk vormgegeven. Deze problemen maken het paper niet onbegrijpelijk, maar voorkomen wel dat het als stilistisch sterk of bijna foutloos kan gelden. Daarom passend in de voldoende tot licht bovengemiddelde range.

intro_feedback: The introduction clearly states a relevant research question and hypothesis, addresses societal relevance early, and includes all 4 required articles (Anderson, Kampmann, Bouchard, plus a self-found adolescent-focused article). Key concepts such as SAS, VRET, CGT, and exposure mechanisms are defined, and there is a visible theoretical framework using Emotional Processing Theory and Inhibitory Learning Theory. Prior studies are generally connected to the current question rather than only summarized, and the final transition to the design choice and follow-up rationale is explicit. This places the paper above Tier 2. I do not place it higher than the bottom of Tier 3 because the line of reasoning is not consistently tight: some claims are overstated or not fully well-supported (e.g., strong claims about VRET working 'vooral gedragsmatig', or Kahlon being treated as if it directly tested the same combination design), and the theoretical integration is somewhat uneven. Still, the argument is coherent overall and the design choice is explicitly justified relative to prior gaps, which supports a 7.5.
methods_feedback: The Methods section is broadly coherent with the RQ and hypotheses and contains the required subsections. Participants are described with sample size, mean age, SD, gender counts, recruitment, inclusion/exclusion criteria, allocation by randomization, and compensation information. Materials include descriptions of both conditions and the main questionnaire (LSAS-CA) with reference, scale content, scoring, and cut-off information. Procedure gives a basic chronological overview from diagnostic interview to measurement moments. This satisfies Tier 2 core criteria overall. I do not place it in Tier 3 because there are still substantial omissions/inconsistencies: the procedure is too brief and does not describe the study from start to finish in enough detail; some material/procedure information is mixed; the SCID-5 lacks a proper reference and fuller measurement description; standardization across conditions is only partly described; and there is limited detail on how sessions were conducted across all eight weeks. Replication would be possible only at a general level, not with strong clarity. Therefore 6.5 is appropriate.
results_feedback: The section identifies an appropriate statistical test for the design (mixed ANOVA), reports descriptive statistics, includes an outlier check, mentions assumption checks, and reports the main effects and interaction with p-values. There is also a demographics table, a means/SD table, and a figure is referenced. However, the section falls short of Tier 2 because several core reporting elements are incomplete or insufficiently correct. Most importantly, the ANOVA results omit degrees of freedom entirely (e.g., F(2, ) and F(1, )), which is a substantial omission; the tables are poorly formatted and incomplete/confusing; the demographic table conflicts with the participant description (non-binary participants appear in Results but not in Methods); assumption checks are asserted very generally rather than clearly reported; and the follow-up is inconsistently referred to as both 3 months and 12 months. Post-hoc reporting is present but not fully precise. Because the section has the essentials but lacks the completeness expected from the sample and rubric, a Tier 1 grade of 6.0 is most justified.
discussion_feedback: The discussion clearly revisits the RQ, addresses whether the hypothesis was supported, and interprets the findings at construct level. It compares findings to prior studies from the introduction, discusses an unexpected long-term pattern, revisits the theoretical framework, includes specific limitations, and proposes concrete future research directions. Broader practical and societal implications are also discussed. This places the section solidly in Tier 2. I do not place it in Tier 3 because some reasoning is not fully coherent or data-grounded. In particular, the interpretation of the long-term findings is somewhat inconsistent with the reported means and with the earlier statement that VRET+CGT had a larger pre-follow-up drop; the discussion sometimes overstates what can be concluded from the results; and alternative interpretations are only partly considered. The structure is good and the content is clearly above passing, but the evaluation of the theory and the impact of limitations on the conclusions is not consistently deep enough for Tier 3. A 7.0 fits best.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally understandable and uses scientific language appropriately for the level. The overall structure follows the expected paper format, and most paragraphs have a discernible focus. Referencing is present throughout. At the same time, there are frequent language and APA issues: punctuation and spacing errors, inconsistent naming (e.g., SAS/SAD, CGT+VRET/VRET+CGT), awkward phrasing, grammar problems, citation inconsistencies, and several formatting issues in both the text and reference list. Some sentences are overly long or imprecise, and transitions are sometimes rough. These issues do not usually obscure meaning, so the paper is still adequate rather than insufficient. Because the writing is clear enough overall but not polished, 6.5 is appropriate.

intro_feedback: The introduction clearly states a relevant research question and hypothesis, addresses societal relevance early, and includes all four required articles (Anderson, Kampmann, Bouchard, plus an additional article focused on adolescents). The overall line of reasoning is present and mostly coherent: the paper moves from the burden of social anxiety disorder, to theoretical explanations for exposure, to prior findings on VRET and combined treatments, and then to the specific gap concerning adolescents and long-term effects. Theoretical framing is present and linked to the variables through Emotional Processing Theory and Inhibitory Learning Theory, and the final design choice (follow-up, no waitlist) is explicitly justified. methods_feedback: The methods section is broadly coherent with the research question and hypotheses, and the main required subsections are present. intro_feedback: The introduction presents a clear topic, establishes societal relevance early, defines key concepts, and builds toward a relevant research question. The general line of reasoning is coherent: VRET works, existing studies focus on therapist-guided formats, socially anxious individuals may face barriers in face-to-face treatment, and self-guided VRET may be especially useful. methods_feedback: The method is coherent and broadly aligned with the stated research question and hypothesis. The main design is understandable: three conditions, pre-post measurement, randomized assignment, and LSAS as the main outcome. Participants, materials, and procedure are all present. At the same time, the section is only nearly complete rather than fully complete. Important details are missing or insufficiently specified for replication, such as mean age and SD by the full sample in Participants, stronger justification for inclusion/exclusion criteria, and clearer information about allocation procedures. The phrase 'by using AI (coinflip)' is not an adequate scientific description of randomization. The treatment conditions are also somewhat imbalanced and not well justified: self-guided participants complete 14 daily 30-minute sessions, whereas therapist-guided participants receive only 4 sessions across the same period, which creates a major comparability issue that is not addressed. The waitlist condition is only briefly described. In Materials, the LSAS description is too minimal for the writing guide standard: no example item, no scoring range, and no cutoff reference explanation beyond eligibility. Procedure also includes the planned statistical analysis, which belongs less naturally there. So the method is understandable and mostly correct, but important omissions and design-comparability issues keep it at a developing-to-adequate level.
results_feedback: The Results section follows the expected overall structure reasonably well: sample statement, a demographics table, the main ANOVA, descriptive means by condition and time, and post-hoc testing. For example, the text first states that the difference between conditions at post-measurement was significant, but then says there was no significant difference between self-guided and therapist-guided VRET at post-assessment; this suggests that the significant post-test difference likely refers to inclusion of the waitlist, but this is not clearly stated. Assumption checks are minimal and not fully aligned with the sample standard, and Figure 1 is mentioned but not actually provided in the text. Still, the chosen analysis broadly matches the design and the main conclusions can be followed. Because the section is relevant and partly complete but contains notable inconsistencies and statistical reporting weaknesses, it falls at the lower end of passing.
discussion_feedback: The discussion gives a clear answer to the research question and states that both active treatments reduced social anxiety, while the main hypothesis was not supported. Overall, the reasoning is correct and mostly coherent, with relevant critical reflection, but it is not as fully integrated with theory and prior literature as a stronger discussion would be.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally readable and structured in the expected scientific format, with clear section headings and mostly understandable paragraphs. The section does have several weaknesses that prevent a higher score. The inclusion/exclusion criteria are only lightly justified. In Materials, the LSAS is described only partially: the scale reference, number of items, and broad scoring interpretation are given, but there is no sample item, no full scoring range, and no cut-off reference beyond the eligibility threshold. The waitlist condition is barely described as a condition in Materials. The intervention descriptions are understandable but not equally detailed, and standardization between conditions is not addressed clearly. In Procedure, some analysis information is introduced, which does not belong there according to the guide. Overall, the section is adequate and sufficiently complete for this level, but it lacks the precision, placement, and detail needed for Tier 3.
results_feedback: The Results section identifies an appropriate overall analysis for the stated design and reports descriptive statistics for the main outcome at the operational level. A demographics table and a means table are included, and an outlier check is mentioned. These features support a passing grade. However, the section does not clearly meet Tier 2. Statistical reporting is incomplete and in places incorrect or unclear: the ANOVA results omit degrees of freedom formatting and test statistics are reported without the necessary commas/equal signs, making it hard to evaluate them properly. Assumption checks are insufficiently complete for this design; only normality is mentioned, while other relevant assumptions for repeated-measures ANOVA are not reported. Post-hoc reporting is inconsistent: the section states both that the post-measurement difference was significant and later that there was no significant difference between self-guided and therapist-guided VRET at post-assessment, which creates interpretive confusion. There is also a likely copy error referring to 'PCL-5 scores' instead of LSAS. In addition, Figure 1 is announced but not actually shown in the provided text. Because the reporting is understandable enough to convey the main pattern but falls short of the completeness and consistency expected for Tier 2, this section is best graded in Tier 1.
discussion_feedback: The discussion clearly revisits the aim and hypothesis, states the main conclusion, and interprets the findings at the construct level. It connects back to the introduction and compares the findings to prior studies, including both the expected effectiveness of therapist-guided and self-guided VRET and the unexpected lack of a difference between them. The theoretical idea involving self-efficacy is revisited, and the student does attempt to explain the unexpected result by considering advantages of therapist guidance. Two study-specific limitations are discussed with reasonable specificity, and future research suggestions follow from those limitations. This satisfies Tier 2 well. The section does not fully reach Tier 3 because the reasoning, while coherent, is not consistently deep or critical. Comparisons to prior research are present but somewhat surface-level, and the theoretical framework is revisited more by restating expectations than by explicitly evaluating whether the data support, challenge, or refine the self-efficacy account. The broader societal implications are touched on mainly in the conclusion rather than fully argued in the discussion itself. Still, for this course level, the section shows solid scientific reasoning and engages with the non-significant difference rather than ignoring it, which is a strength.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally clear, readable, and organized into recognizable scientific sections. Most paragraphs have a discernible focus, and scientific language is used appropriately for the level. Grammar and spelling errors are present but not frequent enough to seriously interfere with comprehension. APA referencing is mostly functional. This fits Tier 2. The score is not higher because there are several style and formatting issues throughout: awkward phrasing, occasional redundancy, inconsistent punctuation and spacing in citations, some sentence-level errors, and several APA inconsistencies in both in-text citations and the reference list. There are also occasional imprecise formulations and small wording problems that reduce polish. Still, the text remains understandable and reasonably structured throughout, so the writing is adequate to good for this student level.

intro_feedback: The introduction clearly states a research question and hypothesis, addresses societal relevance, defines key concepts such as social anxiety, VRET, and self-efficacy, and includes the three core articles plus additional literature. The overall line of reasoning is present and mostly logical: the paper moves from the societal problem, to VRET as an intervention, to the gap concerning self-guided VRET, and then to the prediction. Scientific relevance is also argued rather than only mentioned. This places the section solidly in Tier 2. However, it does not fully reach Tier 3. The prior studies are connected, but often still in a somewhat summary-like way rather than consistently functioning as tightly integrated building blocks. The theoretical framework is present, but the link from self-guidance to greater self-efficacy to better SA outcomes is somewhat assumed rather than strongly substantiated, and the design justification relative to prior research gaps could be more explicit and precise. There are also some inaccuracies or looseness in describing prior studies (e.g., how the core studies are characterized), which weakens the argument somewhat. Overall, this is a clear and above-average introduction for this level, but not yet fully convincing and seamless enough for the Good tier.
methods_feedback: The Methods section is coherent with the stated research question and contains the required subsections. Participants are described with sample size, recruitment strategy, inclusion criteria, mean age, gender distribution, random assignment, and compensation. Materials includes the main dependent measure with reference, item count, scale description, and general interpretation of higher scores, and both intervention conditions are described in a broadly understandable way. The procedure is chronological and gives a reasonable overview from eligibility screening through assignment and intervention to post-measurement. This satisfies Tier 2 overall. The section does not clearly reach Tier 3 because several required details are still missing or underdeveloped. The LSAS description lacks full scoring details and interpretation of minimum/maximum scores. The wait-list condition is barely described as a condition. Some important methodological details remain vague, such as exactly how randomization was implemented, whether the therapist-guided protocol was standardized across therapists, and how adherence in the self-guided condition was tracked. There is also some mixing of design/analysis information into the Procedure, and some materials-level detail appears unevenly distributed. So the section is adequate and reasonably replicable at student level, but not detailed enough for a stronger score.
results_feedback: The Results section reports a relevant statistical analysis aligned with the design, includes descriptive statistics at the operational level, reports means and SDs, includes a demographics table and an outcome table, mentions an outlier check, and reports the main effects and interaction with p-values. This is enough for Tier 1. However, the section does not fully meet Tier 2 criteria. Although assumption checking is mentioned, it is incomplete and too limited for the repeated-measures ANOVA expected here: only normality is mentioned, while other relevant assumptions such as homogeneity and sphericity are not reported. The reporting of the test statistics is also incomplete or incorrect-looking, because the F statistics are missing proper degrees of freedom formatting and are not presented clearly enough. Post-hoc reporting is present, but incomplete and somewhat inconsistent: one sentence says the post-measurement difference was significant, but then another sentence says there was no significant difference between self-guided and therapist-guided VRET at post-assessment. Also, the text mistakenly refers to PCL-5 instead of LSAS, which suggests carryover from a template and reduces confidence in the precision of reporting. Figure 1 is announced but not actually shown in the provided paper text. Overall, this is a passing results section with the expected general structure, but the incompleteness and internal inconsistencies keep it below adequate-to-good range.
discussion_feedback: The discussion revisits the aim and hypothesis, states the main conclusion, and interprets the findings at the construct level. It clearly addresses that both active conditions reduced social anxiety symptoms and that the hypothesis that self-guided VRET would outperform therapist-guided VRET was not supported. The section compares findings to prior studies from the introduction and offers an explanation for the unexpected lack of difference between the two active conditions, namely that therapist guidance may provide compensatory benefits. It also includes two specific limitations and corresponding future research suggestions, and ends with a broader implication regarding accessibility and viability of self-guided VRET. These features place the section in Tier 2. It does not fully reach Tier 3 because the reasoning is not consistently developed in a fully coherent, integrated way across the whole discussion. The theoretical framework is revisited, but only somewhat briefly; the paper does not really evaluate whether the self-efficacy account is supported, challenged, or in need of revision in a deeper way. The comparison to prior research is meaningful but still somewhat limited, and the implications could be more explicitly tied back to the societal relevance from the introduction. Also, the discussion would be stronger if it reflected more critically on the unexpectedly stronger numerical reduction in the therapist-guided condition and on the limitations of drawing strong conclusions from the current design. Still, this is a solid, above-average discussion for this course level.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally understandable and uses scientific language appropriately overall. The structure is clear, with recognizable sections and mostly focused paragraphs. Referencing is present throughout and mostly functional. This supports a Tier 2 score. However, the writing contains a noticeable number of grammar, punctuation, formatting, and APA inconsistencies that prevent a higher grade. There are several awkward phrasings, spacing errors, capitalization inconsistencies, repeated wording, and occasional unclear or imprecise sentences. Some examples include inconsistent terminology (SA vs SAD vs social anxiety), citation formatting problems, duplicated punctuation, and minor layout issues in tables and headings. There is also some redundancy in the argumentation, especially in the discussion. The paper remains readable, but it is not polished enough for Tier 3, where language and APA would need to be rare-error and consistently precise.

intro_feedback:
The introduction presents a clear and relevant research question and generally follows a coherent line of reasoning from societal relevance to theory, prior research, and hypotheses. The societal relevance is established early and linked to relapse and long-term treatment effectiveness. The theoretical framework is stronger than average for this level: the student explains SAD maintenance through Clark & Wells / Rapee & Heimberg and links exposure to the Inhibitory Learning Model, then uses this theory to justify the expectation of stronger long-term effects for VRET. The required studies are included and used in service of the argument. The final transition to the research question, hypotheses, and design is clear. 

What keeps this from a higher grade is that the literature integration is somewhat uneven. Several empirical claims are overstated or insufficiently nuanced, especially where the text presents VRET as clearly improved or more accessible without consistently grounding this in the cited evidence. Some relevance arguments are broad and occasionally speculative. There are also a few inaccuracies or weaker links, such as using a non-SAD-specific paper for treatment limitations and some repetition across paragraphs. Overall, though, the reasoning is coherent, the RQ is well motivated, and the section is convincingly argued for this course level.
methods_feedback:
The method is coherent and clearly aligned with the stated research question and hypotheses. The core design is understandable: a randomized comparison of VRET and IVE with pre-, post-, and 6-year follow-up measurements. Participants, materials, and procedure are all present, and the random assignment is described. The SIAS is described with developer citation, item count, response scale, score range, and example item, which matches the writing guide reasonably well. The intervention descriptions are also fairly concrete and allow the reader to understand what distinguishes the two conditions.

The main weaknesses are incompleteness and some internal inconsistency. In Participants, the paper states that no distinction was made between men and women, but the Results section later reports gender ratios per condition. Important sample details are missing from Methods, such as gender composition by condition. Inclusion and exclusion criteria are present, but some are too absolute or insufficiently justified, for example excluding any second DSM diagnosis. The procedure is mostly chronological, but some material/procedure boundaries blur slightly. The method also lacks some details that would strengthen replicability, such as who administered the diagnosis, whether the SIAS was completed online or in person at each wave, and how therapist standardization was handled. Still, for this student level, the section is mostly complete and correct.
results_feedback:
The results section is structured well and is close to the sample format expected in the course. It includes a demographics table, a table with means and standard deviations per condition and timepoint, the main mixed ANOVA, assumption reporting, and post-hoc comparisons. The reporting is understandable and aligned with the design. The interpretation of the statistical pattern is also generally correct: no baseline difference, improvement in both groups post-treatment, then divergence at long-term follow-up.

This section is around the expected course benchmark for a solid Results section, but not clearly above it. A few issues prevent a higher grade. The reporting is not fully precise: the sentence 'Dit zorgde voor een significant verschil tussen de condities op de posttest' appears to refer to the 6-year follow-up and is therefore likely a labeling error. Assumption checks are stated very briefly and without the detail shown in the sample, and effect sizes are absent. Statistical formatting is not fully APA-consistent throughout. Also, the results would have been stronger with explicit reference to the figure in the text. Still, the analyses and reporting are mostly correct, complete, coherent, and relevant.
discussion_feedback:
The discussion is the strongest section of the paper. It opens with a clear answer to the research question, explicitly states which hypotheses were and were not supported, and distinguishes well between short-term and long-term findings. The student does more than restate results: they interpret the long-term divergence between VRET and IVE and connect it back to the Inhibitory Learning Model. The section also engages with an unexpected finding, namely the absence of a short-term superiority effect for VRET, and offers a plausible interpretation grounded in theory and prior research. This is exactly the kind of scientific reasoning the rubric values.

The critical reflection is relevant and reasonably specific. The limitations on comorbidity and therapist effects are meaningful and tied to interpretation and generalizability rather than being purely generic. The practical implications are also linked back to the introduction and to the actual findings.

What keeps the grade from being even higher is that some interpretations remain a bit confident relative to the evidence. For example, the explanation for continued symptom reduction after VRET is plausible but speculative, and broader practical claims about accessibility and effectiveness are stated strongly given the hypothetical single-study design. There is also limited reflection on additional possible alternative explanations for a 6-year pattern, such as life events, subsequent treatment, or attrition-related issues. Still, this is a coherent, well-argued, above-average discussion for this level.
lang_style_feedback:
The paper is generally readable and structured clearly, with recognizable sections and mostly logical paragraphing. Scientific language use is mostly appropriate for a second-year student, and the reader can follow the main line of argument without much difficulty. References are generally used responsibly, and the paper shows a reasonable command of academic style.

That said, there are several language and style issues that keep this from a higher score. There are noticeable grammar and wording problems in Dutch, including agreement errors, awkward phrasing, repetition, and occasional imprecise formulations. Some sentences are long and could be more concise. APA style is acceptable but not consistently neat: capitalization in journal titles is irregular, some reference formatting is inconsistent, and there are minor reporting/labeling issues in the text. There are also a few vague or overstated claims, especially in the introduction and conclusion. Overall, the style is mostly correct and functional, but not polished.

intro_feedback: De introductie heeft een duidelijke en logische opbouw van maatschappelijke relevantie naar theorie, eerdere literatuur, onderzoeksgat en uiteindelijk de onderzoeksvraag en hypotheses. De onderzoeksvraag is helder, relevant en goed verbonden aan het probleem van terugval op lange termijn. Ook worden de verplichte kernartikelen (Anderson, Kampmann, Bouchard) correct gebruikt en aangevuld met een extra studie. Sterk is dat er daadwerkelijk een theoretisch kader wordt opgebouwd met Clark & Wells, Rapee & Heimberg en vooral het Inhibitory Learning Model, en dat dit model ook wordt gebruikt om de langetermijnhypothese te motiveren. Wel blijft de literatuurintegratie soms nog wat beschrijvend in plaats van echt synthetiserend, en sommige claims zijn wat stellig of onvoldoende scherp onderbouwd (bijv. dat VRET 'daardoor' een verbeterde behandelmethode is, of uitspraken over toegankelijkheid en volhouden). Daarnaast is één bron minder passend: Henning et al. lijkt niet specifiek over SAD te gaan, wat de precisie van de argumentatie iets verzwakt. Toch is de rode draad duidelijk en overtuigend voor dit niveau.
methods_feedback: De methode is coherent en sluit goed aan bij de onderzoeksvraag en hypothesen. De belangrijkste onderdelen zijn aanwezig: deelnemers, materiaal en procedure. Er is informatie over leeftijd, steekproefgrootte, randomisatie, inclusie/exclusiecriteria, vergoeding en informed consent. Ook worden beide interventies redelijk concreet beschreven en is de SIAS voldoende uitgelegd met aantal items, schaal en scorebereik. Voor dit niveau is de methode dus grotendeels compleet en begrijpelijk. Tegelijk ontbreken enkele elementen die volgens de schrijfwijzer eigenlijk wel verwacht worden. De geslachtsverdeling ontbreekt in de deelnemerssectie zelf en wordt pas in de resultaten gegeven; dat is methodologisch onhandig. De inclusie/exclusiecriteria zijn deels te grof of onrealistisch geformuleerd, bijvoorbeeld het volledig uitsluiten van depressie en 'een andere stoornis' zonder verdere onderbouwing. Er ontbreekt ook informatie over hoe de SAD-diagnose precies is vastgesteld, door wie, en met welk instrument of interview. Verder staat een deel van de procedure van de SIAS al onder materiaal, en de beschrijving van standaardisatie tussen condities had nog explicieter gekund. Daardoor is de methode degelijk maar niet sterk uitgewerkt.
results_feedback: De resultaten volgen duidelijk de structuur van het voorbeeld: eerst steekproefbeschrijving, daarna analyse, assumpties, hoofdeffecten/interactie en vervolgens post-hoc toetsen. Er zijn twee tabellen opgenomen met demografie en uitkomstmaten per conditie en meetmoment, wat goed aansluit bij de verwachtingen. De gekozen analyse (mixed ANOVA) past bij het beschreven design. De kernbevindingen worden helder en begrijpelijk gerapporteerd, en de resultaten zijn relevant voor de onderzoeksvraag. Vergeleken met de kalibratie ligt dit rond of iets boven het baseline-niveau van een nette studentversie van de sample results. Er zijn wel enkele onnauwkeurigheden. In Tabel 1 wordt een geslachtsverdeling gerapporteerd terwijl in de methode stond dat er geen onderscheid was gemaakt tussen man en vrouw; dat is inconsistent. Ook staat in de post-hoc beschrijving waarschijnlijk per ongeluk 'significant verschil tussen de condities op de posttest (p < .001)' terwijl dit gezien de context de follow-up moet zijn. Daarnaast blijven assumptiechecks erg summier en worden geen effectgroottes gerapporteerd. Dat zijn tekortkomingen, maar voor dit niveau blijft de sectie grotendeels correct, compleet en coherent.
discussion_feedback: De discussie is sterk op studentniveau. De eerste alinea geeft een duidelijke hoofdconclusie, koppelt die expliciet aan de hypotheses en maakt netjes onderscheid tussen ondersteunde en niet-ondersteunde verwachtingen. Daarna worden de belangrijkste bevindingen inhoudelijk geïnterpreteerd en teruggekoppeld aan theorie en eerdere literatuur. Vooral de koppeling aan het Inhibitory Learning Model is functioneel in plaats van alleen decoratief, en de student probeert ook het onverwachte kortetermijnresultaat te verklaren. Dat past goed bij de rubricfocus op wetenschappelijke redenering. Ook bevat de discussie relevante beperkingen die redelijk studiespecifiek zijn, zoals beperkte generaliseerbaarheid door exclusie van comorbiditeit en mogelijke therapeut-effecten. De implicaties voor praktijk en toekomstig onderzoek vloeien logisch voort uit de bevindingen. Verbeterpunten zijn dat sommige interpretaties vrij speculatief worden geformuleerd zonder sterke empirische onderbouwing, bijvoorbeeld waarom VRET na zes jaar nog verder verbetert. Daarnaast had de theoretische reflectie nog kritischer gekund: welke delen van het theoretisch model zijn nu echt getest en welke niet? Ook wordt Arnfred et al. vrij positief gebruikt, terwijl de titel van die studie juist op underpowered resultaten wijst; dat had kritischer besproken kunnen worden. Desondanks is de redenering coherent, relevant en overtuigend voor dit niveau.
lang_style_feedback: De tekst is over het algemeen goed leesbaar en wetenschappelijk van toon. De structuur van de secties is duidelijk en de lezer kan de lijn van het betoog goed volgen. Ook zijn de meeste paragrafen thematisch afgebakend en functioneel voor de argumentatie. Er zijn wel meerdere taal- en formuleringstekortkomingen die maken dat dit niet boven gemiddeld uitkomt op stijl. Er staan geregeld grammaticale of stilistische fouten in de tekst, zoals incongruente werkwoordsvormen, onhandige formuleringen en soms informeel of net niet precies taalgebruik. Ook zijn er verschillende APA- en referentieonzuiverheden, bijvoorbeeld in bronvermelding, hoofdletters in tijdschrifttitels en kleine inconsistenties in namen/jaartallen. Verder zijn sommige zinnen wat lang of redundant, en enkele claims zijn te stellig geformuleerd voor wetenschappelijk schrijven. De stijl belemmert het begrip niet, maar is ook niet near-faultless.

intro_feedback: De introductie bevat een duidelijke maatschappelijke relevantie, definieert SAD en motiveert waarom langetermijneffecten van behandeling belangrijk zijn. Er is ook een herkenbare lijn naar de onderzoeksvraag, met bespreking van theorie (Clark & Wells, Rapee & Heimberg, Inhibitory Learning Model) en de verplichte kernartikelen. De hypothesen en het design worden aan het einde helder genoemd. Sterk is dat de tekst probeert theorie expliciet te koppelen aan verschillen tussen VRET en IVE op lange termijn. Tegelijk blijft de argumentatie op sommige punten wat stellig of speculatief, bijvoorbeeld waar VRET al vrij overtuigend als ‘verbeterde’ methode wordt neergezet voordat de literatuur dat volledig draagt. De literatuur wordt meer als opeenvolgende samenvatting dan als echt geïntegreerde synthese gebruikt, en sommige relevantie-argumenten zijn wat zwakker onderbouwd of niet helemaal populatiespecifiek. Ook is er een kleine inhoudelijke slordigheid in de bronkeuze rond beperkingen/comorbiditeit en een referentie die niet optimaal aansluit bij SAD. Al met al is de introductie coherent en boven gemiddeld, maar nog niet heel overtuigend uitgewerkt op het niveau van synthese en precisie.
methods_feedback: De methode is coherent en sluit goed aan op de onderzoeksvraag en hypothesen. De hoofdonderdelen deelnemers, materiaal en procedure zijn aanwezig, en het design is duidelijk: twee condities, pre-post-follow-up, randomisatie. Positief is dat inclusie/exclusiecriteria, werving, randomisatie en compensatie worden genoemd. De beschrijving van de SIAS is ook voldoende concreet, met aantal items, schaal, voorbeelditem en scorebereik. De interventies worden begrijpelijk beschreven en er is aandacht voor vergelijkbaarheid tussen condities doordat beide 10 sessies van 40 minuten hebben. Tegelijk ontbreken een paar elementen die volgens de schrijfwijzer eigenlijk wel verwacht worden of preciezer hadden gekund. Zo wordt in de deelnemerssectie expliciet gezegd dat geen onderscheid is gemaakt tussen man en vrouw, terwijl demografische verdeling wel verwacht wordt en later in de resultaten alsnog verschijnt. Ook blijven diagnostische procedure en operationalisatie van de DSM-5-diagnose vrij vaag, en is niet volledig duidelijk hoe therapieprotocollen zijn gestandaardiseerd om confounds te beperken. Verder staat procedureel gebruik van de SIAS deels onder Materiaal. Desondanks is de methode voor dit niveau goed navolgbaar en grotendeels compleet.
results_feedback: De resultatensectie volgt de verwachte structuur vrij goed en lijkt duidelijk geïnspireerd op het voorbeeld: eerst beschrijvende steekproefinformatie, daarna de mixed ANOVA, gevolgd door post-hocvergelijkingen. Er is een demografische tabel en een tabel met gemiddelden per conditie en meetmoment, wat voor dit vak belangrijk is. De analyses sluiten aan op het design en worden over het algemeen correct en begrijpelijk gerapporteerd. Ook is de interpretatie van het interactie-effect helder. Een pluspunt is dat de gerapporteerde patronen logisch aansluiten op de hypothesen en later gebruikt kunnen worden in de discussie. Er zijn wel enkele onnauwkeurigheden. De assumptiecontrole is erg summier in vergelijking met het voorbeeld; er wordt alleen gesteld dat aan aannames is voldaan zonder onderbouwing. Daarnaast zit er een duidelijke fout in de tekst: aan het einde van de post-hocbeschrijving staat dat het significante verschil tussen condities op de 'posttest' werd gevonden, terwijl gezien de context de 6-jaar follow-up bedoeld wordt. Zulke inconsistenties verlagen de precisie, maar de sectie blijft als geheel volledig en voldoende coherent. Daarom is dit een nette, iets bovengemiddelde resultatensectie.
discussion_feedback: De discussie begint sterk met een duidelijke beantwoording van de onderzoeksvraag en een expliciete terugkoppeling naar de hypothesen. De student onderscheidt netjes welke verwachting wel en niet is ondersteund, en bespreekt ook de onverwachte bevinding dat VRET en IVE op korte termijn vergelijkbaar waren. Daarnaast wordt geprobeerd om de resultaten te verbinden aan de theorie uit de introductie, vooral het Inhibitory Learning Model, en aan eerdere studies. Ook bevat de discussie relevante beperkingen die redelijk studiespecifiek zijn, zoals beperkte generaliseerbaarheid door uitsluiting van comorbiditeit en mogelijke therapeut-effecten. Dat is positief. Tegelijk blijft een deel van de interpretatie wat speculatief, bijvoorbeeld de verklaring dat deelnemers VRET makkelijker zelfstandig zouden blijven toepassen in het dagelijks leven; dat volgt niet direct uit de data. De theoretische implicaties hadden ook nog preciezer gekund: de theorie wordt vooral bevestigend gebruikt, maar minder kritisch geëvalueerd of bijgesteld. Verder zijn de bredere implicaties soms wat stellig geformuleerd, alsof de studie al definitief aantoont dat VRET terugval vermindert. Ondanks die punten is de discussie coherent, relevant en duidelijk boven adequaat voor dit niveau.
lang_style_feedback: De tekst is over het algemeen goed leesbaar en logisch opgebouwd, met duidelijke secties en een herkenbare wetenschappelijke stijl. De meeste alinea’s hebben een duidelijk onderwerp en de lijn van het betoog is doorgaans goed te volgen. Voor een tweedejaarsstudent is dit taalniveau solide. Er zijn wel meerdere taal- en formuleringselementen die iets minder sterk zijn. Zo zijn er geregeld grammaticale of stilistische slordigheden, zoals congruentiefouten, wat onnatuurlijke formuleringen en soms informele of te stellige bewoordingen. Ook is er enige redundantie, vooral waar voordelen van VRET herhaald worden. APA is redelijk verzorgd, maar niet foutloos: enkele referenties of bronkeuzes zijn minder passend, terminologie wisselt soms, en statistische rapportage is niet overal helemaal strak. Dit alles belemmert het begrip niet sterk, maar voorkomt wel een hogere stijlscore.

intro_feedback: The introduction clearly meets Tier 2 and reaches Tier 3 overall. The research question is explicit, the hypotheses are stated, societal relevance is addressed early, and all 4 required articles are present (Anderson, Kampmann, Bouchard, plus Arnfred). Key concepts such as SAD, relapse, IVE, and VRET are defined. There is also a recognizable theoretical framework: the Clark & Wells / Rapee & Heimberg models are linked to maintenance mechanisms, and the Inhibitory Learning Model is used to explain why exposure should work and why VRET might differ from IVE in the long term. Prior studies are not merely listed; they are connected to the argument about short- versus long-term evidence. The design choice (long-term comparison between VRET and IVE) is explicitly justified from a gap in prior research. This supports a Tier 3 score. The grade does not go higher because the line of reasoning is not fully tight throughout: some claims about VRET being more accessible, cheaper, easier to sustain, and likely superior are asserted somewhat strongly relative to the evidence discussed, and a few transitions remain closer to study-summary than fully seamless building-block reasoning. Scientific relevance is present, but the argument could be more sharply formulated around exactly what prior studies did and did not establish. Overall, this is a good, above-average introduction with a clear argumentative line.
methods_feedback: The Methods section is coherent and clearly related to the stated RQ, so it comfortably passes Tier 1 and just reaches Tier 2. Participants are described with sample size, mean age and SD, inclusion/exclusion criteria, allocation to conditions, and compensation. Materials include the main dependent measure with reference, number of items, response scale, sample item, and scoring interpretation. Both intervention conditions are described in understandable detail, and the procedure is chronological from recruitment to 6-year follow-up. Randomization is also specified. These are strong Tier 2 features. However, the section does not reach Tier 3. A key reason is that some required participant information is inconsistent or incomplete across sections: the Participants subsection says no distinction was made between men and women, while the Results table later gives a full gender distribution. That inconsistency weakens completeness. In addition, questionnaire coverage is minimal because only one instrument is described, and although that may be the sole measure, there is little extra detail such as cut-offs or psychometric information. Some methodological choices are only briefly justified, and standardization across conditions to reduce confounds is not described in much detail. There is also some procedural content mixed into Materials, especially around therapist interaction in VRET. Overall, the section is solid and adequate, but not yet fully polished or complete enough for Tier 3.
results_feedback: The Results section clearly exceeds Tier 1 and fits Tier 2 overall. The correct statistical test for the design is identified (mixed ANOVA), main effects and the interaction are reported with test statistics and p-values, descriptive statistics are given at the operational level, and tables/figure are included. A demographics table is present, a means/SD table per condition and timepoint is present, an outlier check is reported, assumptions are mentioned, and Holm-corrected post-hoc tests are described. This aligns well with the course expectations for an adequate Results section. The section does not fully reach Tier 3. Although assumptions are said to be met, they are reported only globally and not completely or specifically at the level modeled in the sample results section; the reader is not shown how normality/homogeneity/sphericity were checked or any actual values.
